title: Reconcile agent semantic contracts registry row by row
description:
Background: REG-AGENT-CONTRACTS-001 owns reconciliation of the agent semantic contracts registry. The following is the complete normative registry snapshot captured from registries/AGENT_CONTRACTS.md during the 2026-08-31 plan-to-bead audit (65 registered rows). It is embedded so an implementer does not need the source Markdown to understand the planned contract; the active machine-readable generation and digest remain the highest truth tier.

--- BEGIN EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---
# Agent contract registry

Semantic protocol: `fss/1`. Machine umbrella: `architecture/agent_contracts.json`.

The registry separates knowledge state, provenance class, hypothesis disposition, access transformation, and operation outcome. Stable IDs are never renumbered.

## Semantic narrow waist

Every subsystem reaches the agent compositor through the internal `CognitiveFacet` contract owned
by `fss-agent-core`. Required coordinates are: facet/owner identity; basis anchor and high-water;
scope/validity; knowledge cells; coverage/health; contradictions/unknowns; evidence handles; open
obligations and indeterminate effects; resource state/full cost; affordance seeds; invalidators and
degradation; proof and continuation. Facets are capability/privacy projected before composition and
carry no effect authority. The machine contract is `subsystemProjectionContract` in
`architecture/agent_contracts.json`.

## Knowledge states

Knowledge-state permission is deliberately split. An estimate may support speculative planning, but it cannot authorize an irreversible effect merely by having a high score.

| ID | State | Meaning | May support planning | May authorize irreversible effect | Explicit assumptions required |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `KSTATE-001` | `known` | The proposition is established for the named anchor and validity scope by admissible evidence or a proved terminal postcondition. | yes | yes, subject to capability and policy | no |
| `KSTATE-002` | `estimated` | The proposition is supported by a declared derivation or model with explicit uncertainty and operating-envelope limits. | yes | no | yes |
| `KSTATE-003` | `unknown` | The authorized evidence acquired so far does not establish the proposition. | yes, as an explicit branch or open variable | no | yes |
| `KSTATE-004` | `conflicted` | Material admissible evidence supports incompatible propositions or generations. | yes, only as competing branches | no | yes |
| `KSTATE-005` | `stale` | The proposition was valid only at an older anchor or generation and has not been revalidated. | yes, only as a revalidation candidate | no | yes |
| `KSTATE-006` | `not_observable` | The declared sensor/authorization/model domain could not have established the proposition for the requested interval. | yes, as a protected residual possibility | no | yes |
| `KSTATE-007` | `redacted` | The proposition or its evidence exists but is intentionally withheld by the current privacy/capability projection. | yes, only through non-leaking abstract constraints | no | yes |
| `KSTATE-008` | `indeterminate` | A consequential external outcome may have occurred but is not yet proved or safely negated. | yes, only in reconciliation branches | no | yes |
| `KSTATE-009` | `not_applicable` | The proposition has no meaning for the named object, scope, or lifecycle state. | no | no | no |

## Provenance classes

| ID | Class | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `PROV-001` | `observed` | Directly supported by canonical sensor, device, operator, or effect evidence. |
| `PROV-002` | `derived` | Deterministically computed from named canonical inputs under a registered algorithm and generation. |
| `PROV-003` | `predicted` | Counterfactual or forward prediction under an explicit branch/model and assumptions. |
| `PROV-004` | `remembered` | Advisory operational memory or prior episode material that must be revalidated against live evidence. |
| `PROV-005` | `operator_asserted` | A human/operator assertion with identity, time, scope, and later corroboration status. |
| `PROV-006` | `vendor_claimed` | Metadata or state asserted by a device/vendor boundary and not treated as independent physical truth. |
| `PROV-007` | `policy` | A rule, threshold, capability, or privacy decision from an exact policy generation. |

## Hypothesis dispositions

`live` · `supported` · `disfavored` · `refuted` · `resolved` · `superseded`

Hypothesis disposition is not a knowledge state. A hypothesis can be `disfavored` while some of its propositions remain `known`; a `refuted` hypothesis does not turn missing observations into falsehood.

## Public semantic operations

Every operation uses the universal request/response envelopes; the table exposes the typed request payload selected by the sole machine operation registry.

| ID | Operation | Owner | Mode | Default view | Typed request payload | Effectful | Durable | Gate | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `AOP-001` | `session.open` | `fss-agent-session` | `session_control` | `AVIEW-002` | `fss.agent_mission.v1` | no | yes | `QL-AGENT-001` | `specified` |
| `AOP-002` | `session.resume` | `fss-agent-session` | `session_control` | `AVIEW-006` | `fss.agent_handoff_capsule.v1` | no | yes | `QL-AGENT-001` | `specified` |
| `AOP-003` | `session.orient` | `fss-situation` | `read` | `AVIEW-002` | `fss.agent_query_plan.v1` | no | no | `QL-AGENT-001` | `specified` |

## Object composition

- **`ContractBasis`:** pins the exact semantic and registry universe used to interpret an agent artifact.
- **`AgentRequestEnvelope`:** wraps every public operation request with contract basis, lifecycle identity, anchor/workspace preconditions, view, targets, typed payload, budget, requested authority/privacy, continuation, idempotency, hydration/compression policy, and taint.
- **`MissionContract`:** contains one ObjectiveContract and immutable revisions of focus, assumptions, budgets, and terminal criteria.
- **`WorldEnvelope`:** separates the nominal world, certified core and absences, material alternative worlds, adversarial residuals, common invariants, unresolved dimensions, and discriminating affordances.
- **`SituationCapsule`:** contains a SituationFrame with a WorldEnvelope, optional MeaningfulDelta, active investigations/plans/obligations, resource state, a categorized control envelope, ContextPack, and SemanticCompressionReceipt.
- **`InvestigationCase`:** contains or references a HypothesisWorkspace, discriminating probes, stop rules, findings, and residual uncertainty.
- **`ControlPlan`:** contains a witnessed contingent DAG and prepared domain effects; it never confers authority by itself.
- **`ExperienceCapsule`:** summarizes one or more ExecutionEpisodes and can produce advisory FeedbackProposal or LearningProposal objects.
- **`HandoffCapsule`:** publishes the minimum sufficient mission/workspace/case/plan/obligation state as a root-last portable graph.
- **`AgentResponseEnvelope`:** wraps every public operation result; an AgentCognitiveEnvelope or SituationCapsule is a typed payload, never a competing transport contract.

## Request/response rule

Every `AOP-*` operation accepts `fss.agent_request_envelope.v1` and returns
`fss.agent_response_envelope.v1`. `architecture/agent_operations.json` alone names the
operation-specific request payload schema. An incompatible ContractBasis fails closed; transports
may omit unqualified operations but cannot redefine parameters or payload meaning.

## Evidence–possibility–control envelope

Every primary driver publication answers three different questions without collapsing them:

1. **Evidence envelope:** what the current anchor and coverage witnesses positively establish, including certified absences.
2. **Possibility envelope:** which materially different or adversarial worlds remain compatible with evidence, authorization, and observability limits.
3. **Control envelope:** which affordances are robust across the protected possibility envelope, which are conditional on named worlds, which gather information, which wait, and which are blocked.

A high-consequence residual world is never removed because it ranks poorly. It leaves the envelope only when a named witness, policy, or explicit scope change rules it out.

## Resource URI templates

```text
fss://deployment/{deployment}/anchor/{anchor}
fss://deployment/{deployment}/situation/{capsule}
fss://deployment/{deployment}/sensor/{sensor}
fss://deployment/{deployment}/zone/{zone}
fss://deployment/{deployment}/event/{event}/revision/{revision}
fss://deployment/{deployment}/case/{case}/revision/{revision}
fss://deployment/{deployment}/hypothesis/{hypothesis}
fss://deployment/{deployment}/evidence/{digest}
fss://deployment/{deployment}/plan/{plan}
fss://deployment/{deployment}/obligation/{obligation}
fss://mission/{mission}/revision/{revision}
fss://session/{session}/workspace/{workspace}
fss://session/{session}/handoff/{root}
fss://experience/{capsule}
fss://doctor/{bundle}
```
--- END EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---

Approach:
1. Preserve every stable row identity, field meaning, status, scope, owner, cross-reference, prohibition and compatibility rule from the snapshot; reconcile it against the active machine registry and record any later drift explicitly.
2. Map each row to owning crates/planes, schemas, operations/views/resources, requirements, implementation symbols, deterministic reference behavior, fault/negative tests, cost/SLO rows, qualification lanes, proof bundles and public claim impact.
3. Generate Rust types and lookup/validation tables from the canonical registry where appropriate; do not hand-maintain transport-specific vocabularies. Unknown, superseded and tombstoned identities fail explicitly.
4. Validate uniqueness, stable ordering, cross-registry references, authority/privacy/effect separation, immutable generations, bounded costs, and compatibility/migration behavior. A changed meaning requires a versioned successor/ADR, never in-place reinterpretation.
5. Generate human/robot documentation and examples from the same semantic source and retain a deterministic coverage/drift report.

Why this exists: broad subsystem beads can accidentally cover only the happy path. Row-level reconciliation makes the exact agent semantic contracts contract executable and prevents code, tests, documents, transports or status from silently diverging.

The active registry either matches this snapshot or has an explicit versioned drift finding and migration/ADR; no silent deletion, renumbering or weakening is allowed. Automated tests reject duplicates, dangling/illegal references, unknown IDs, incompatible status/meaning changes, authority/privacy/effect leakage, missing proof and transport/doc divergence. title: Reconcile dependency constitution classes registry row by row
description:
Background: REG-DEPENDENCIES-001 owns reconciliation of the dependency constitution classes registry. The following is the complete normative registry snapshot captured from registries/DEPENDENCIES.md during the 2026-08-31 plan-to-bead audit (5 registered rows). It is embedded so an implementer does not need the source Markdown to understand the planned contract; the active machine-readable generation and digest remain the highest truth tier.

--- BEGIN EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---
# Dependency registry

The normative doctrine is [`docs/DEPENDENCY_CONSTITUTION.md`](../docs/DEPENDENCY_CONSTITUTION.md); the machine allowlist is `architecture/dependency_allowlist.toml`.

| ID | Class | Rule | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DEP-OWNED-001` | Owned runtime and Franken-suite families | admitted after per-mechanism integration gate | `Production` |
| `DEP-FUND-001` | serde / serde_json | control-plane schemas only; never durable bytes or authority | `Production subject to audit` |
| `DEP-LAB-001` | Pinned codec/model/vendor/reference executables | sealed fixture/oracle lanes only; no production invocation path and absent from release closure | `Development/migration only` |
| `DEP-ORACLE-001` | Python/reference ecosystems | held-out conformance and lab fixtures only; absent from release closure | `Development only` |
| `DEP-EXCEPTION-001` | Any other external crate | requires DEP record, ADR, source/feature census, semantic owner, substitute prohibition, and removal plan | `Not admitted` |

No exception is implied by appearance in `Cargo.lock`. Release qualification computes and records the complete source/feature closure and fails closed on unknown provenance.
--- END EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---

Approach:
1. Preserve every stable row identity, field meaning, status, scope, owner, cross-reference, prohibition and compatibility rule from the snapshot; reconcile it against the active machine registry and record any later drift explicitly.
2. Map each row to owning crates/planes, schemas, operations/views/resources, requirements, implementation symbols, deterministic reference behavior, fault/negative tests, cost/SLO rows, qualification lanes, proof bundles and public claim impact.
3. Generate Rust types and lookup/validation tables from the canonical registry where appropriate; do not hand-maintain transport-specific vocabularies. Unknown, superseded and tombstoned identities fail explicitly.
4. Validate uniqueness, stable ordering, cross-registry references, authority/privacy/effect separation, immutable generations, bounded costs, and compatibility/migration behavior. A changed meaning requires a versioned successor/ADR, never in-place reinterpretation.
5. Generate human/robot documentation and examples from the same semantic source and retain a deterministic coverage/drift report.

Why this exists: broad subsystem beads can accidentally cover only the happy path. Row-level reconciliation makes the exact dependency constitution classes contract executable and prevents code, tests, documents, transports or status from silently diverging.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 embedded rows are accounted for exactly once in a deterministic coverage manifest with unchanged identity and semantics, plus owner, schema/code symbols, tests, costs/SLOs, lane/gate, retained proof and claim status. title: Reconcile effect identities and outcome semantics registry row by row
description:
Background: REG-EFFECTS-001 owns reconciliation of the effect identities and outcome semantics registry. The following is the complete normative registry snapshot captured from registries/EFFECTS.md during the 2026-08-31 plan-to-bead audit (20 registered rows). It is embedded so an implementer does not need the source Markdown to understand the planned contract; the active machine-readable generation and digest remain the highest truth tier.

--- BEGIN EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---
# Effect registry

Every effect has prepare, revalidate, commit, observe, verify, cancel, and reconcile semantics.

| ID | Effect | Reversibility | Required verification | v1 disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EFFECT-ALERT-001` | send event alert | compensable by correction, not retractable | durable provider receipt or explicit indeterminate | target |
| `EFFECT-ACK-001` | acknowledge/annotate event | supersedable | canonical event annotation revision | target |
| `EFFECT-PTZ-001` | move camera PTZ | normally reversible | observed pose/scene and restore obligation | future after standards baseline |
| `EFFECT-CAMERA-SETTING-001` | change imaging/bitrate/audio/event settings | reversible where old value known | readback + stream-generation rollover | future |
| `EFFECT-SPOTLIGHT-001` | temporary light/siren control | reversible, physically observable | device state and timeout restore | disabled by default |
| `EFFECT-RETENTION-001` | change retention policy | prospective; deletion may be irreversible | policy revision and affected-object plan | target admin path |
| `EFFECT-ARCHIVE-PUBLISH-001` | publish encrypted archive root | additive | root/child/retrievability proof | target |
| `EFFECT-ARCHIVE-DELETE-001` | delete/cryptographically erase archive | irreversible | closure proof or blocked reason | target admin path |
| `EFFECT-EXPORT-001` | create/share evidence package | disclosure irreversible | root, recipient, access/expiry receipt | target admin path |
| `EFFECT-PRIVACY-MASK-001` | change capture/redaction mask | reversible prospectively | rendered preview + policy revision + coverage impact | target admin path |
| `EFFECT-MODEL-ACTIVATE-001` | activate model/index generation | reversible by rollback | atomic generation readback + shadow proof | target |
| `EFFECT-CALIBRATION-ACTIVATE-001` | activate calibration certificate | reversible | exact certificate generation and residual gate | target |
| `EFFECT-ADAPTER-UPGRADE-001` | activate adapter/firmware compatibility tuple | reversible by rollback | shadow/soak receipt | target |
| `EFFECT-REPAIR-001` | mutate ledger/object state per sealed plan | potentially irreversible | revalidation, mutation receipts, post-doctor | target |
| `EFFECT-DRONE-FLIGHT-001` | command drone mission | physically consequential | separate flight-safety system | forbidden in v1 |
| `EFFECT-OFFENSIVE-001` | pursue, restrain, harm, or deploy weapon | dangerous | none acceptable | forbidden |
| `EFFECT-AGENT-MISSION-001` | create/supersede mission objective/constraint contract | supersedable; history immutable | published mission revision and affected-workspace invalidation | target |
| `EFFECT-AGENT-WORK-CLAIM-001` | reserve/release a bounded collaborative work claim | lease-expiring and releasable | claim revision, fence, expiry, and release receipt | target |
| `EFFECT-AGENT-FEEDBACK-001` | append correction/outcome/learning proposal | additive and supersedable | immutable evidence-linked proposal; no activation side effect | target |
| `EFFECT-AGENT-HANDOFF-001` | publish/accept a recipient-scoped handoff root | additive; revocable prospectively | closure proof, recipient acceptance/rebase receipt, and expiry | target |
--- END EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---

Approach:
1. Preserve every stable row identity, field meaning, status, scope, owner, cross-reference, prohibition and compatibility rule from the snapshot; reconcile it against the active machine registry and record any later drift explicitly.
2. Map each row to owning crates/planes, schemas, operations/views/resources, requirements, implementation symbols, deterministic reference behavior, fault/negative tests, cost/SLO rows, qualification lanes, proof bundles and public claim impact.
3. Generate Rust types and lookup/validation tables from the canonical registry where appropriate; do not hand-maintain transport-specific vocabularies. Unknown, superseded and tombstoned identities fail explicitly.
4. Validate uniqueness, stable ordering, cross-registry references, authority/privacy/effect separation, immutable generations, bounded costs, and compatibility/migration behavior. A changed meaning requires a versioned successor/ADR, never in-place reinterpretation.
5. Generate human/robot documentation and examples from the same semantic source and retain a deterministic coverage/drift report.

Why this exists: broad subsystem beads can accidentally cover only the happy path. Row-level reconciliation makes the exact effect identities and outcome semantics contract executable and prevents code, tests, documents, transports or status from silently diverging.
acceptance_criteria: All 20 embedded rows are accounted for exactly once in a deterministic coverage manifest with unchanged identity and semantics, plus owner, schema/code symbols, tests, costs/SLOs, lane/gate, retained proof and claim status. The active registry either matches this snapshot or has an explicit versioned drift finding and migration/ADR; no silent deletion, renumbering or weakening is allowed. Automated tests reject duplicates, dangling/illegal references, unknown IDs, incompatible status/meaning changes, authority/privacy/effect leakage, missing proof and transport/doc divergence. Generated Rust/API/CLI/MCP/TUI/report surfaces and documentation resolve to the same registry digest.

title: Reconcile stable errors and recovery guidance registry row by row
description:
Background: REG-ERRORS-001 owns reconciliation of the stable errors and recovery guidance registry. The following is the complete normative registry snapshot captured from registries/ERRORS.md during the 2026-08-31 plan-to-bead audit (44 registered rows). It is embedded so an implementer does not need the source Markdown to understand the planned contract; the active machine-readable generation and digest remain the highest truth tier.

--- BEGIN EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---
# Stable error registry

Errors are machine identities with structured fields. Human text can improve without changing the
contract. Cancellation and panic remain distinct outcome channels; indeterminate effects are
operation states rather than generic errors.

| ID | Meaning | Retry policy |
|---|---|---|
| `ERR-AUTH-DENIED-001` | principal lacks exact capability | do not retry without new authority |
| `ERR-SECRET-UNAVAILABLE-001` | secret handle cannot be resolved | repair/rotate; bounded retry if provider transient |
| `ERR-DEVICE-UNSUPPORTED-001` | exact product/firmware/app tuple not certified | fail closed or explicit import-only mode |
| `ERR-FIRMWARE-DRIFT-001` | observed device generation differs from registry | disable/move to shadow; no optimistic retry |
| `ERR-ADAPTER-PROTOCOL-001` | adapter response violates typed protocol | terminate adapter generation; retain fixture |
| `ERR-STREAM-NO-FIRST-FRAME-001` | adapter accepted but no decodable frame before budget | reconnect or fail; never claim coverage |
| `ERR-STREAM-CONTINUITY-001` | gaps/jitter exceed contract | degrade coverage; bounded recovery |
| `ERR-CLOCK-UNCERTAIN-001` | capture interval too wide for requested operation | degrade/abstain/recalibrate |
| `ERR-DECODE-001` | media decode failed | preserve source; alternate decoder only if registered |
| `ERR-DECODE-BOUNDS-001` | media exceeds declared bounds | fail closed |
| `ERR-MODEL-UNAVAILABLE-001` | model generation not runnable | route to registered fallback or degrade |

title: Reconcile full operation-cost rows registry row by row
description:
Background: REG-OPERATION-COSTS-001 owns reconciliation of the full operation-cost rows registry. The following is the complete normative registry snapshot captured from registries/OPERATION_COSTS.md during the 2026-08-31 plan-to-bead audit (33 registered rows). It is embedded so an implementer does not need the source Markdown to understand the planned contract; the active machine-readable generation and digest remain the highest truth tier.

--- BEGIN EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---
# Operation cost registry

Machine source: `architecture/operation_cost_registry.toml`.

| Cost ID | Unit | Mandatory semantic work | Key variables |
|---|---|---|---|
| `COST-ACQUIRE-001` | segment | adapter receive, timestamp bound, packet index, content digest, ledger reserve, object stage, root publish | source bytes, packet count, loss reorder, durability barriers |
| `COST-RTSP-001` | stream second | session keepalive, packet receive, rtcp update, continuity accounting, bounded buffer | packets, jitter, loss, auth refresh |
| `COST-PARSE-001` | access unit | framing, parameter epoch, syntax parse, bounds validate, index publish | bytes, nal or obu count, syntax depth |
| `COST-DECODE-001` | megapixel frame | reference resolve, entropy decode, inverse transform, prediction, reconstruction, color output | codec profile, bit depth, pixels, reference count |
| `COST-PROXY-001` | source second | remux or decode, scale, encode, segment, publish | decoded pixels, encoded pixels, codec generation, cpu or accelerator seconds |
| `COST-QUALITY-001` | frame | health features, blur exposure occlusion, tamper state, receipt | pixels, history window |
| `COST-DETECT-001` | candidate batch | preprocess, model execute, postprocess, publish result | pixels, batch, model generation, kernel plan |
| `COST-TRACK-001` | frame track set | predict, gate, assign, update, retire, publish delta | active tracks, detections, assignment edges |
| `COST-ASSOC-001` | association window | transition candidates, feature compare, temporal gate, k best assign, publish hypotheses | tracklets, candidate edges, k, graph size |
| `COST-ANALYZE-001` | candidate window | quality gate, motion gate, detect, track, associate, temporal reason, independent verify, calibrate, adjudicate | frames, pixels, active tracks, model invocations, cpu or accelerator seconds |
| `COST-GRAPH-001` | algorithm run | pin projection, authorize projection, execute reference or optimized, emit witness, shape output | n, m, algorithm operations, output size |
| `COST-SEARCH-001` | query | pin generation, exact filter, lexical candidates, graph expand, semantic refine, score ledger, shape output | documents, candidate count, graph edges, model calls, tokens |
| `COST-EVENT-001` | event revision | collect witnesses, revalidate, policy evaluate, reserve, publish, notify | evidence edges, negative domains, policy rules |
| `COST-ALERT-001` | alert attempt | prepare, idempotency reserve, dispatch, observe receipt, retry or reconcile, verify | channels, payload bytes, retry count |
| `COST-ARCHIVE-001` | published gibibyte | chunk, encrypt, repair encode, remote stage, verify children, publish root, retrievability sample | bytes, objects, repair ratio, put head operations, egress, retrieval |
| `COST-ATP-001` | transferred gibibyte | plan, manifest verify, fetch, repair if needed, object verify, closure verify, root publish | bytes, objects, paths, loss, repair symbols |
| `COST-RETRIEVE-001` | challenge | select samples, remote range get, verify, record, schedule repair | sample bytes, objects, providers, latency |
| `COST-DELETE-001` | deletion plan | authorize, enumerate reachability, delete children, verify absence, publish tombstone | reachable objects, providers, indexes, replicas |
| `COST-CALIBRATE-001` | calibration session | ingest, synchronize, feature track, geometry infer, bundle adjust, covariance, coverage compute, certificate publish | frames, camera count, track count, optimizer iterations |
| `COST-TWIN-001` | mapping session | select frames, pose estimate, depth or gaussian reconstruct, fuse, quality check, publish | frames, pixels, points or gaussians, iterations |
| `COST-MODEL-IMPORT-001` | model generation | verify source, lower ir, canonicalize tensors, static analyze, oracle compare, quality eval, repair encode, publish | operators, tensor bytes, corpus examples, oracle runs |
| `COST-QUERY-001` | query | anchor, structured filter, search, graph projection, fusion, memory pack, evidence shape | rows, candidates, graph operations, tokens, model calls |
| `COST-CHECKPOINT-001` | checkpoint | freeze anchor, materialize state, seal replay tail, verify, publish root | state bytes, delta count, indexes |
| `COST-RELEASE-001` | release matrix | clean snapshot, resolve sibling closure, run lanes, build targets, package, sign, upload, download verify, publish root | targets, lanes, test time, artifact bytes |
| `COST-ORIENT-001` | orientation | pin anchor, restore or create workspace, construct situation frame, construct world envelope, compute meaningful delta, select knowledge cells, construct control envelope, construct affordance frontier, compress with receipt, emit situation capsule | ledger rows, delta count, graph operations, search candidates, tokens, evidence handles |
| `COST-FOLLOW-001` | delta delivery | validate cursor, consume authority deltas, classify decision impact, coalesce safe updates, preserve nondroppable updates, emit continuation | delta count, subscribers, classification work, output tokens |
| `COST-CONTEXT-001` | context pack | pin frame, apply capability privacy projection, score decision relevance, select submodular items, record omissions, emit compression receipt, publish pack | candidate items, evidence edges, tokens, hydration bytes, graph operations |
| `COST-INVESTIGATE-001` | case revision | pin case and anchor, refresh hypotheses, attach support and contradiction, predict observations, rank discriminating probes, apply stop rule, publish revision | hypotheses, evidence edges, candidate probes, model calls, graph operations, tokens |
| `COST-AFFORDANCE-001` | affordance frontier | enumerate registered operations, filter authority privacy safety, estimate value cost risk, remove dominated, sensitivity check, canonical order | candidate actions, preconditions, policy rules, counterfactuals |
| `COST-AGENT-PLAN-001` | control plan | freeze objective, pin frame case generations, enumerate steps, attach witnesses, type effect boundaries, add contingencies and stop rules, seal decision digest | steps, dependencies, witnesses, effect families, counterfactual branches |
| `COST-EXPLAIN-001` | explanation | resolve decision, collect provenance, compute minimal support subgraph, retain contradictions and omissions, shape view, emit expansion handles | evidence edges, decision nodes, counterfactuals, tokens |
| `COST-HANDOFF-001` | handoff | freeze workspace, select minimum sufficient state, apply recipient projection, materialize children, verify closure and expiry, publish root, accept and rebase | cases, plans, obligations, evidence handles, tokens, object bytes |
| `COST-ACCRETE-001` | learning proposal | freeze episode basis, collect outcome attribution, compare prediction to result, classify applicability, extract candidate, collect counterexamples and harm, run trauma guard, run held out validation, decide promote reject expire, publish advisory proposal and receipt | episodes, evidence edges, counterexamples, historical candidates, fixtures, validation runs, tokens, model calls, operator review seconds |

No SLO is accepted until its cost row can derive the denominator and identify all mandatory work. Provider pricing belongs in dated manifests, not these semantic rows.
--- END EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---

Approach:
1. Preserve every stable row identity, field meaning, status, scope, owner, cross-reference, prohibition and compatibility rule from the snapshot; reconcile it against the active machine registry and record any later drift explicitly.
2. Map each row to owning crates/planes, schemas, operations/views/resources, requirements, implementation symbols, deterministic reference behavior, fault/negative tests, cost/SLO rows, qualification lanes, proof bundles and public claim impact.
3. Generate Rust types and lookup/validation tables from the canonical registry where appropriate; do not hand-maintain transport-specific vocabularies. Unknown, superseded and tombstoned identities fail explicitly.
4. Validate uniqueness, stable ordering, cross-registry references, authority/privacy/effect separation, immutable generations, bounded costs, and compatibility/migration behavior. A changed meaning requires a versioned successor/ADR, never in-place reinterpretation.
5. Generate human/robot documentation and examples from the same semantic source and retain a deterministic coverage/drift report.

Why this exists: broad subsystem beads can accidentally cover only the happy path. Row-level reconciliation makes the exact full operation-cost rows contract executable and prevents code, tests, documents, transports or status from silently diverging.
acceptance_criteria: All 33 embedded rows are accounted for exactly once in a deterministic coverage manifest with unchanged identity and semantics, plus owner, schema/code symbols, tests, costs/SLOs, lane/gate, retained proof and claim status. The active registry either matches this snapshot or has an explicit versioned drift finding and migration/ADR; no silent deletion, renumbering or weakening is allowed. Automated tests reject duplicates, dangling/illegal references, unknown IDs, incompatible status/meaning changes, authority/privacy/effect leakage, missing proof and transport/doc divergence. Generated Rust/API/CLI/MCP/TUI/report surfaces and documentation resolve to the same registry digest.

title: Reconcile publication states and primitives registry row by row
description:
Background: REG-PUBLICATION-PRIMITIVES-001 owns reconciliation of the publication states and primitives registry. The following is the complete normative registry snapshot captured from registries/PUBLICATION_PRIMITIVES.md during the 2026-08-31 plan-to-bead audit (13 registered rows). It is embedded so an implementer does not need the source Markdown to understand the planned contract; the active machine-readable generation and digest remain the highest truth tier.

--- BEGIN EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---
# Publication primitive registry

Machine source: `architecture/publication_primitives.json`. Publication is a semantic effect, not a successful write call. Every primitive reserves identity, materializes unpublished children, verifies closure, exposes the root last, and retains a receipt.

| ID | Primitive | Owner | Root invariant | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PUB-AUTH-001` | `authority_generation` | `fss-publication` | No reader observes a root whose children are incomplete | `specified` |
| `PUB-OBJECT-001` | `archive_object_graph` | `fss-custody` | Remote object existence alone is not publication | `specified` |
| `PUB-SEARCH-001` | `search_generation` | `fss-search` | Provisional searchable state is explicitly marked non-durable | `specified` |
| `PUB-GRAPH-001` | `graph_projection` | `fss-graph-store` | Projection declares consumed authority high-water mark | `specified` |
| `PUB-MODEL-001` | `model_activation` | `fss-model-registry` | Downloaded or merely loadable model is not active | `specified` |
| `PUB-CAL-001` | `calibration_activation` | `fss-geometry` | Low residual without held-out/coverage checks is insufficient | `specified` |
| `PUB-ADAPTER-001` | `adapter_compatibility_profile` | `fss-adapter-registry` | Device-family success never generalizes across firmware/app tuples | `specified` |
| `PUB-EVIDENCE-001` | `evidence_bundle` | `fss-evidence` | Human report and machine manifest publish atomically | `specified` |
| `PUB-DELETE-001` | `deletion_closure` | `fss-privacy` | Deletion success requires alternate-index/cache reachability closure | `specified` |
| `PUB-RELEASE-001` | `release_root` | `fss-release` | Partial target success cannot bless an aggregate release | `specified` |
| `PUB-AGENT-WORKSPACE-001` | `agent_workspace_revision` | `fss-agent-session` | A resumable workspace never references missing cases, plans, obligations, or evidence handles and never hides invalidated state | `specified` |
| `PUB-AGENT-HANDOFF-001` | `agent_handoff_capsule` | `fss-handoff` | A handoff is not complete until the recipient can reconstruct mission, uncertainty, obligations, continuations, and invalidations without hidden conversational state | `specified` |
| `PUB-AGENT-EXPERIENCE-001` | `agent_experience_capsule` | `fss-episode` | Learning never rewrites the original episode and no proposal is promoted without its immutable outcome basis | `specified` |
--- END EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---

Approach:
1. Preserve every stable row identity, field meaning, status, scope, owner, cross-reference, prohibition and compatibility rule from the snapshot; reconcile it against the active machine registry and record any later drift explicitly.
2. Map each row to owning crates/planes, schemas, operations/views/resources, requirements, implementation symbols, deterministic reference behavior, fault/negative tests, cost/SLO rows, qualification lanes, proof bundles and public claim impact.
3. Generate Rust types and lookup/validation tables from the canonical registry where appropriate; do not hand-maintain transport-specific vocabularies. Unknown, superseded and tombstoned identities fail explicitly.
4. Validate uniqueness, stable ordering, cross-registry references, authority/privacy/effect separation, immutable generations, bounded costs, and compatibility/migration behavior. A changed meaning requires a versioned successor/ADR, never in-place reinterpretation.
5. Generate human/robot documentation and examples from the same semantic source and retain a deterministic coverage/drift report.

Why this exists: broad subsystem beads can accidentally cover only the happy path. Row-level reconciliation makes the exact publication states and primitives contract executable and prevents code, tests, documents, transports or status from silently diverging.

The active registry either matches this snapshot or has an explicit versioned drift finding and migration/ADR; no silent deletion, renumbering or weakening is allowed. Automated tests reject duplicates, dangling/illegal references, unknown IDs, incompatible status/meaning changes, authority/privacy/effect leakage, missing proof and transport/doc divergence. Generated Rust/API/CLI/MCP/TUI/report surfaces and documentation resolve to the same registry digest.

title: Reconcile risk ledger and mitigations registry row by row
description:
Background: REG-RISKS-001 owns reconciliation of the risk ledger and mitigations registry. The following is the complete normative registry snapshot captured from registries/RISKS.md during the 2026-08-31 plan-to-bead audit (18 registered rows). It is embedded so an implementer does not need the source Markdown to understand the planned contract; the active machine-readable generation and digest remain the highest truth tier.

--- BEGIN EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---
# Risk registry

| ID | Risk | Mitigation and release consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `RISK-VENDOR-001` | proprietary firmware/app breaks adapter | exact tuple, simulator, shadow qualification, fail closed, maintenance owner |
| `RISK-SDK-001` | desired drone/camera absent from official SDK | import/display bridge only; no native/autonomy claim |
| `RISK-CODEC-001` | hostile media triggers a defect or resource attack in the pure-Rust decoder | checked arithmetic, bounded arenas, scalar oracle, malformed-media corpus, cancellation budgets, source quarantine, fail-closed capability promotion |
| `RISK-MODEL-001` | VLM hallucination/poor calibration misses threat | cascade, independent verifier, event metrics, abstention, never direct effects |
| `RISK-CORRELATION-001` | multiple cameras/vendor cloud share failure domain | failure-domain graph and independent local sensors |
| `RISK-TIME-001` | clock/buffering error corrupts association | interval time, marker calibration, degradation thresholds |
| `RISK-GEOMETRY-001` | attractive but inaccurate 3D twin | certificate residuals/covariance/held-out validation; renderings derived |
| `RISK-COVERAGE-001` | static coverage map hides live failure | effective coverage includes continuity/quality/calibration health |
| `RISK-PRIVACY-001` | system over-collects household/bystander data | local-first, early masks, minimization, deletion closure, identity off |
| `RISK-SECRET-001` | vendor/archive credentials leak through logs/prompts | secret handles, process domains, redaction tests, support-bundle policy |
| `RISK-ARCHIVE-001` | cheap archive costs explode via tiny objects/retrieval | operation-cost registry, chunking, dated price manifest, audit |
| `RISK-RECOVERY-001` | crash leaves ambiguous alert/control/archive effect | operation receipts, obligations, reconcile before retry |
| `RISK-DATASET-001` | test leakage/property bias creates false quality | property/session split, sealed holdout, subgroup slices, new generations |
| `RISK-BIOMETRIC-001` | identity feature becomes surveillance network | disabled default, property-local TTL, explicit enrollment, no cross-property |
| `RISK-AGENT-001` | agent overreach or prompt injection from sensor text | read-first capabilities, taint, no shell/vendor proxy, prepared effects |
| `RISK-DEPENDENCY-001` | broad or foreign runtime stack undermines the pure-Rust product | closed universe, exact import contracts, release-closure census, foreign tools restricted to sealed oracle lanes, ADR/audit |
| `RISK-COMPLEXITY-001` | architecture delays usable vertical slice | deterministic replay/UVC walking skeleton, gate-ordered work, no substitute seams |
| `RISK-GUARANTEE-001` | “never miss” language creates false assurance | defined distributions, confidence bounds, negative evidence, explicit observability |
--- END EMBEDDED REGISTRY SNAPSHOT ---

Approach:
1. Preserve every stable row identity, field meaning, status, scope, owner, cross-reference, prohibition and compatibility rule from the snapshot; reconcile it against the active machine registry and record any later drift explicitly.
2. Map each row to owning crates/planes, schemas, operations/views/resources, requirements, implementation symbols, deterministic reference behavior, fault/negative tests, cost/SLO rows, qualification lanes, proof bundles and public claim impact.
3. Generate Rust types and lookup/validation tables from the canonical registry where appropriate; do not hand-maintain transport-specific vocabularies. Unknown, superseded and tombstoned identities fail explicitly.
4. Validate uniqueness, stable ordering, cross-registry references, authority/privacy/effect separation, immutable generations, bounded costs, and compatibility/migration behavior. A changed meaning requires a versioned successor/ADR, never in-place reinterpretation.
5. Generate human/robot documentation and examples from the same semantic source and retain a deterministic coverage/drift report.

Why this exists: broad subsystem beads can accidentally cover only the happy path. Row-level reconciliation makes the exact risk ledger and mitigations contract executable and prevents code, tests, documents, transports or status from silently diverging.
acceptance_criteria: All 18 embedded rows are accounted for exactly once in a deterministic coverage manifest with unchanged identity and semantics, plus owner, schema/code symbols, tests, costs/SLOs, lane/gate, retained proof and claim status. The active registry either matches this snapshot or has an explicit versioned drift finding and migration/ADR; no silent deletion, renumbering or weakening is allowed. Automated tests reject duplicates, dangling/illegal references, unknown IDs, incompatible status/meaning changes, authority/privacy/effect leakage, missing proof and transport/doc divergence. Generated Rust/API/CLI/MCP/TUI/report surfaces and documentation resolve to the same registry digest.

title: Realize decision-card families and evidence-bearing explanations
description:
Background: REG-DECISION-CARDS-001 owns the decision-card families and evidence-bearing explanations defined by architecture/decision_cards.json. The complete planning snapshot captured on 2026-08-31 is embedded below so future implementation does not depend on remembered prose. The active file/digest remains highest-tier truth; any later difference is explicit drift requiring reconciliation.

      "id": "DEC-AGENT-PRESSURE-001",

--- END EMBEDDED MACHINE CONTRACT ---

Approach: validate syntax/schema and semantic invariants; preserve stable IDs, versions, tombstones, owner and status; generate typed Rust representations and deterministic validators where applicable; map every entry to owning crates, schemas, operations/views, capabilities/errors/costs, tests, qualification lanes, proof and claims; verify all referenced files/symbols/IDs exist and no undeclared parallel registry appears. Enforce Rust 2024 pinned nightly, #![forbid(unsafe_code)], first-party pure-Rust production semantics, downward ownership, explicit authority/Cx, bounded cancellation-safe work, immutable generations, privacy projection and honest proof strength. Generated docs and human projections derive from the same semantic source. Changes are versioned with migration/ADR and negative drift evidence; they never silently weaken gates.

Reasoning: decision-card families and evidence-bearing explanations determines architecture and claim meaning across subsystems. Embedding the exact contract plus executable reconciliation prevents broad tasks from overlooking an entry and makes later drift diagnosable.
acceptance_criteria: The active architecture/decision_cards.json parses deterministically and every embedded entry is present exactly once or has an explicit versioned drift/migration finding. A generated coverage graph resolves each entry to owner, implementation/schema, positive and negative tests, qualification lane, retained evidence and public-claim impact, with zero duplicates, dangling references, illegal dependencies, undeclared status upgrades or semantic forks. Golden and malformed fixtures validate canonical serialization/config parsing, stable ordering/IDs, compatibility and bounds. The policy/qualification lane consumes the exact current digest and blocks source/doc/code/test/proof disagreement.

title: PROGRAM-RESEARCH — Open research questions and ADR promotion
description:
## Outcome

Own OPEN-001 through OPEN-020 as bounded experiments with competing hypotheses, cost/privacy/license analysis, negative-result retention, and explicit promotion/revival rules.

## Program role

This is a cross-cutting coordinate under the complete FSS program. Its children attach to the relevant work packages and gates; it does not create a rival architectural layer. Work must preserve stable IDs, exact authority anchors, proof-linked status, and the root-last completion doctrine.
acceptance_criteria:
- The epic’s complete contract is represented by granular child beads with explicit owners and true blocking edges.
- Child acceptance covers success and failure semantics, compatibility/migration, privacy/security, performance cost, observability, documentation/status, and retained proof.
- Unit/property, deterministic reference, differential, fault/cancellation/crash, integration, end-to-end, resource-economy, and release lanes are assigned where applicable.
- Closing this epic requires terminal proof for every required child; implementation or schema presence alone is insufficient.

title: OPEN-001 — What is the cheapest cascade that preserves required observable-threat recall?
description:
Research question
What is the cheapest cascade that preserves required observable-threat recall?

Initial bounded experiment
Pareto sweep gating, detector, and temporal stages on sealed development properties.

Required investigation contract
Write at least two competing hypotheses plus a null/unsupported outcome; name shared failure domains, predicted observations, falsifiers, a representative corpus or formal model, measurement uncertainty, privacy and licensing constraints, full compute/operator/storage cost, and a stop rule. Establish the simplest deterministic baseline before optimized or learned variants. Preserve raw evidence identities, exact seeds/configurations/generations, contradictions, excluded strata, and negative results. No experiment grants production authority or silently changes policy, models, thresholds, retention, or public claims.

Decision and accretion
Promote a conclusion to an ADR only when the measurement or proof plan is representative, evidence separates the alternatives, operational/privacy/security costs are explicit, and the decision states scope, confidence, reversibility, expiry triggers, and what result would reopen it.
acceptance_criteria: Competing hypotheses, falsifiers, corpus/proof identity, metrics, budgets, stop rule, and privacy/license review are preregistered; the experiment is reproducible with structured logs and exact digests; baseline and alternatives are compared without hiding unsupported or negative results; decision sensitivity and residual unknowns are reported; any accepted result becomes a reviewed ADR and learning proposal rather than a silent production change.

Cryptographic-erasure and honest-irreversibility contract

Derived indexes are rebuilt/compacted so deleted content cannot resurrect through restore or replay.

title: DOC-033 — Compile natural-language requests into typed, taint-preserving AgentQueryPlans
description:
Background: natural-language input is untrusted intent, never authority. agent_query_plan.v1 requires originalTextDigest, taintSources, alternative interpretations, selectedInterpretation, estimatedCost, and outputView. The compiler must make ambiguity, authority, privacy, evidence scope, cost, and effect boundaries visible before execution.

Approach: implement a deterministic staged compiler: normalize without losing the original digest/spans; label user, retrieved, vendor, model, and tool text by taint/provenance; resolve session symbols and registered resource URIs; produce competing typed interpretations; identify missing authority/coverage and dangerous ambiguity; estimate evidence hydration, model, graph, latency, energy, privacy, and operator costs; preview requested view and capability projection; then either select a provably safe interpretation, request bounded clarification, or return a typed refusal/blocked state. Prompt/control text may propose plans but cannot mint capabilities, change policy, trigger effects, or override registry semantics. Effectful intent yields a prepared witnessed plan only.

Considerations: preserve exact spans for explanations; prevent confused-deputy retrieval and count/rank leaks; keep redacted/not-observable/unknown distinct; bind plans to ContractBasis, SituationFrame/WorldEnvelope, policy and generation digests; ensure replay determinism under equivalent symbol tables.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover parsing, exact-span preservation, stable digests, aliases, ambiguity lattices, cost estimates, URI resolution, and deterministic interpretation selection. title: DOC-034 — Implement session-local symbols, semantic zoom, progressive results, and hydration cache validity
description:
Background: agents need compact stable references without replacing canonical IDs. agent_session.v1 requires symbolTableGeneration and symbols; the operating model requires semantic zoom, progressive results, continuations, and priced evidence hydration. Aliases are session-local conveniences, never durable identity or authority.

Approach: map short aliases to canonical typed resource URIs/digests with creation anchor, generation, visibility, privacy transform, expiry, and invalidators. Rebase or policy/generation drift advances symbolTableGeneration and makes stale aliases fail explicitly. Define registered zoom levels from decision-oriented summary through evidence hydration, each with a SemanticCompressionReceipt, omitted-decision counterfactuals, byte/token/cost estimates, continuation token, and non-droppable classes. Cache hydrated evidence only under exact content digest, authorization/privacy projection, generation and validity basis; never let cached visibility bypass a later clamp. Progressive streams publish root-consistent partial results, preserve terminal/urgent deltas, and identify completeness and silence.

Considerations: aliases must survive harmless presentation changes but never collision, cross-session reuse, or hidden renumbering; large objects move through ATP handles rather than response blobs; cancellation finalizes continuations and cache leases.
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove alias uniqueness, typed URI resolution, generation fencing, rebase behavior, cross-session denial, cache hit/miss semantics, privacy/capability noninterference, deterministic zoom receipts, protected-world preservation, and continuation/resume after cancellation/disconnect. E2E orientation reaches a bounded first-useful answer, progressively hydrates to byte-equivalent evidence, and produces equivalent semantics across transports. Stale/redacted/unauthorized aliases and cache entries fail with stable repair guidance rather than null or silent re-fetch.

title: DOC-035 — Refine Mission into ObjectiveContracts with lexicographic safety clamps and terminal proof
description:
Background: Mission and ObjectiveContract are cross-cutting coordinates for the entire abstraction tower. An objective is not a prose goal or utility score: it declares success, failure, stop, safety, privacy, authority, budget, observability, proof, and handoff conditions against an exact ContractBasis and WorldEnvelope.

Approach: implement deterministic refinement from Mission to immutable ObjectiveContract and bounded child contracts. Evaluate hard constitutional, authorization, privacy, protected-world, retention, and resource clamps lexicographically before soft value. Decompose work only when child success composes into parent success and child failure/stop cannot bypass parent constraints. Bind each contract to stable requirement IDs, authority/capability roots, situation/world digest, budgets, deadlines, evidence/coverage needs, accepted residual risk, supported and unsafe worlds, terminal outcomes, and required proof. Revalidation after drift either yields a new version or invalidates the plan; it never mutates history.

Considerations: distinguish achieved, failed, stopped, blocked, waiting, delegated, indeterminate, and superseded. Recommendations do not grant commit authority. Objective progress must be derivable from canonical evidence and active obligations, not chat.
acceptance_criteria: Schemas and state machines validate every required ObjectiveContract field and legal transition. Property tests prove hard clamps dominate utility, decomposition preserves parent constraints/budgets, stale world or authority roots invalidate rather than silently rebase, and terminal states require matching proof or explicit indeterminacy. E2E cases cover success, failure, stop rule, budget exhaustion, delegation, contradictory evidence, lost effect ACK, and handoff/resume; no active obligation or next step exists only conversationally.

title: DOC-036 — Build the AttentionFrontier, interruption policy, shared attention, role projections, and swarm brief
description:
Background: attention is a typed nondominated frontier after constitutional clamps, not an opaque priority score. It must expose urgent obligations, invalidations, contradictions, protected high-loss worlds, expiring evidence, investigations, value-of-information probes, and resource pressure while supporting human roles and multiple agents without duplicating or hiding work.

Approach: define AttentionItem components for mission relevance, deadline/lease, loss/risk, uncertainty, information value, reversibility, cost, owner, dependencies, invalidators, expected proof, and visibility transform. Hard-clamp forbidden/unauthorized items, Pareto-filter the rest, preserve sensitivity and dominated reasons, and establish deterministic CGSE tie-breaks only for presentation. Define interruption thresholds, coalescing, silence certificates, and terminal/urgent non-coalescible transitions. Shared attention uses immutable findings and fenced WorkClaims; a swarm brief includes common ContractBasis, SituationFrame/WorldEnvelope, work partition, contradictions, shared failure domains, budgets, obligations, merge rules, and resnapshot triggers. Role-shaped views alter projection, never truth.

Considerations: one item may be visible differently to owner, responder, privacy reviewer, auditor, or agent; hidden details cannot leak through counts/ranks; ranking and handoff may not erase protected worlds or urgent obligations.
acceptance_criteria: Reference tests prove hard-clamp and Pareto correctness, deterministic ties, component/sensitivity explanations, interruption/coalescing rules, silence certificates, privacy noninterference, and protected-item retention under compression/view changes. Multi-agent E2E tests cover claim races, lease expiry, duplicate-work reduction, disagreement, immutable finding merge, stale briefs, role projections, agent loss, and handoff. Every surfaced item names why now, owner, cost/risk, invalidators, expected proof, and a valid typed next affordance or terminal reason.

title: DOC-037 — Represent epistemic debt as priced, expiring, handoff-safe mission state
description:
Background: when an agent proceeds under unresolved assumptions, the SituationCapsule and AgentSessionCapsule must carry epistemic debt. Debt is neither generic uncertainty nor a hidden TODO; it records the decision that consumed an assumption, its possible consequence, repayment evidence, owner, cost, deadline, and invalidators.

Approach: define immutable debt entries anchored to EvidenceDeltaBatch, KnowledgeCells, hypothesis disposition, ObjectiveContract, WorldEnvelope, plan/effect/obligation, and originating decision fingerprint. Price probability-independent high-loss exposure as well as expected cost; mark which affordances are robust, conditional, information-gathering, wait/watch, or blocked until repayment. Accrue/age debt deterministically, escalate interruption before expiry or protected-world exposure, close only with witnessed evidence or explicit contract termination, and carry all open debt through workspace, handoff, and semantic compression receipts.

Considerations: model confidence cannot discharge debt; missing coverage cannot repay absence; policy/view changes may increase visibility requirements; learned memory may suggest probes but cannot silently forgive debt.
acceptance_criteria: State-machine and property tests cover creation, accumulation, pricing, ownership transfer, expiry/escalation, contradiction, repayment, invalidation, terminal objective handling, compression, and handoff/resume. E2E scenarios prove debt changes affordance classification and blocks unsafe commit, survives agent/process failure, and can be repaid by exact evidence/coverage. No debt disappears through ranking, view change, resnapshot, merge, or model reranking; every closure carries a proof anchor.

title: DOC-038 — Implement deployment profiles and release channels without semantic forks
description:
Background: the architecture defines five placement profiles—edge-lite, edge-gpu, split-gpu, archive-only, and lab—and four trust channels—reference, lab, canary, stable. Profiles change resource placement and available accelerators/devices, not evidence, authority, privacy, uncertainty, publication, or agent semantics.

Approach: model a versioned DeploymentProfile generation describing host/resources, enabled first-party components, remote executor constraints, network zones, privacy boundary, storage/custody placement, degradation envelope, required qualification lanes, and unsupported capabilities. edge-lite performs standards acquisition, custody and cheap detection with optional authorized verifier; edge-gpu supports local detector/tracker/bounded VLM/geometry; split-gpu uses a trusted pure-Rust executor and ATP for encrypted authorized evidence; archive-only restores/scrubs/searches/reports with no live acquisition; lab isolates vendor/oracle/fault work. Channel promotion is root-last, proof-gated, monotonic in evidence strength, reversible, and separate from build success.

Considerations: unavailable features are typed, not emulated; no profile downloads latest models or hides foreign runtimes; canary does not weaken privacy/effect rules; cross-profile transfer preserves immutable generations and receipts.

Release channels are explicitly reference, lab, canary, and stable; those searchable names remain distinct from the five deployment profiles and from build/qualification state.
acceptance_criteria: Configuration/schema tests reject unknown or semantically divergent profiles and channel transitions. Differential E2E tests replay identical evidence on all compatible profiles and prove equal canonical facts, uncertainties, WorldEnvelope, decision fingerprints, privacy projection, and effect eligibility, with only declared cost/latency/degradation differences. Promotion/rollback tests cover partial publication, stale qualification, revoked artifacts, anti-rollback, split connectivity loss, archive-only effect denial, and lab credential isolation. Support claims name exact profile/channel/platform/device/model generations and proof expiry.

title: DOC-039 — Enforce the integrated mechanical-sympathy and operation-cost doctrine
description:
Background: performance is a semantic contract because latency, copying, allocation, I/O, cache behavior, numerical nondeterminism, and resource pressure can change coverage and decisions. The plan requires separate source/live/cognition paths, an operation-cost row before optimization, and evidence that optimizations preserve the oracle.

Approach: define per-operation budgets and witnesses for bytes read/written, copies, allocations, peak resident memory, queue depth, locks/contention, I/O/syscalls, CPU/GPU time, energy, model/graph work, token cost, privacy exposure, and operator burden. Use zero/low-copy owned buffers on source paths, bounded buffer pools/arenas, columnar hot data, batched durable I/O, and cache policies keyed by immutable generations. Permit narrow flat combining only with bounded wait, cancellation, fairness and ownership proof; permit safe SIMD/kernels only behind deterministic scalar references and registered numeric tolerances. Separate cache admission/eviction from canonical truth. Benchmarks use representative and adversarial fixtures, cold/warm regimes, pressure tiers, and retained raw distributions.

Considerations: faster false results do not count; optimization cannot coalesce terminal transitions or coverage loss; failures and degradation must be measured; benchmark environments and compiler flags are part of provenance.
acceptance_criteria: Every hot operation has a registered cost row, scalar semantic oracle, budget, pressure behavior, and benchmark proof before optimization. Unit/property tests prove pool/arena lifetime, generation-fenced caches, flat-combining fairness/cancellation, bounded channels, no global singleton/lock, numeric tolerance, and output bounds. E2E benchmarks retain raw samples plus p50/p95/p99/max, throughput, accuracy/calibration, coverage loss, energy/privacy/operator burden, environment/toolchain identity, and semantic digests. Regressions or missing cost evidence block the owning lane rather than changing thresholds silently.

title: DOC-040 — Maintain the dated source census, research ledger, licenses, limitations, and import provenance
description:
Background: docs/SOURCE_CENSUS.md and docs/RESEARCH_LEDGER.md capture the external and sibling source DNA behind the design. Research is provenance and rationale, not current implementation truth or blanket import authority.

Approach: for every cited project, standard, protocol, paper, vendor/device tuple, price, model, or tool, record exact URL/repository, immutable revision or publication version, access/as-of date, license and redistribution constraints, specific files/symbols/sections inspected, mechanism learned, limitations/unknowns, shared failure domains, security/privacy implications, and the registry/ADR/import gate that owns any adoption. Preserve negative findings and superseded sources. Automate link/revision/license drift detection without auto-upgrading policy, compatibility, readiness, or architectural status.

Considerations: distinguish primary from secondary/vendor claims, laboratory oracle from production dependency, and current observation from historical note; never record credentials or proprietary protected artifacts.

Naming note: this is the Source Census contract as well as the research-ledger contract; both names must remain searchable and resolve to the same provenance graph.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic census audit covers every external reference in normative plans, deep dives, registries, schemas, manifests, fixtures, and reports with no orphan or ambiguous source. Each adopted mechanism resolves to exactly one IMP-* entry and exact source closure; each non-adopted item states why and what evidence could change the decision. License inventory, source hashes, limitations, as-of dates, link status, and supersession are machine-checkable. Qualification fails on missing/changed license, mutable “latest” source, vanished revision, or undocumented research-to-contract promotion.

title: DOC-041 — Define MediaDerivativeReceipt lineage for every crop, transcode, redaction, and model input
description:

DATA_FORMATS defines a MediaDerivativeReceipt so every crop, resize, colorspace conversion, transcode, clip, thumbnail, privacy mask, enhancement, or model tensor remains linked to source custody or explicitly records omission.

title: DOC-042 — Make DecisionFingerprint construction, replay, and divergence explanation normative
description:
Background: decisions must be later reproducible and comparable. A DecisionFingerprint binds the exact evidence/world/contract/generation and deterministic algorithm basis; it is not merely a hash of the final recommendation.

Approach: canonically encode the request/query plan, Mission and ObjectiveContract, ContractBasis, authority/capability/privacy roots, SituationFrame/WorldEnvelope, evidence and coverage anchors, assumptions/epistemic debt, policies/thresholds, device/model/calibration/config generations, graph projection/algorithm/tie-break/complexity witness, numeric tolerance, random seed/schedule, cost manifest, selected view/compression receipt, affordance frontier, plan and expected proof. Domain-separate and hash the ordered encoding. Replays verify compatible schemas and reconstruct derived state from EvidenceDeltaBatch; mismatches produce a typed field-level divergence report and never masquerade as nondeterminism.

Considerations: equivalent presentations/transports share a fingerprint; a changed evidence anchor must not; redaction may hide values but still prove the authorized digest relationship; retained proprietary bytes may use handles.
acceptance_criteria: Reference vectors and cross-crate/property tests prove canonical ordering, domain separation, collision-resistant composition, schema migration, transport/view equivalence, and sensitivity to every decision-bearing input. Golden replay reproduces fingerprints across clean hosts and schedules where determinism is promised. Fault tests classify missing evidence, incompatible generation, stale policy, unavailable algorithm, numeric tolerance breach, and corrupted receipt. E2E explanations identify the smallest differing inputs and resulting frontier/plan change without leaking redacted data.

title: DOC-043 — Authenticate sensor feeds and model shared tamper, replay, spoof, and cloud failure domains
description:
Background: transport encryption authenticates a channel, not necessarily the physical scene, camera, firmware, timestamp, or cloud-mediated feed. SECURITY requires explicit feed-authenticity and tamper semantics; corroboration claims must account for shared power, network, account, vendor cloud, clock, placement, and attacker failure domains.

Approach: bind source sessions to enrolled device/adapter/firmware/config identities, negotiated protocol parameters, key/certificate or USB topology where available, monotonic sequence/replay windows, clock uncertainty, reconnect epochs, custody roots, and feed-health/tamper observations. Detect duplication, stale loops, discontinuities, impossible timing, content replay, cover/move/dazzle/disconnect/jam signals, and vendor/cloud substitution, while preserving unknown when proof is unavailable. Model shared failure domains explicitly in corroboration and WorldEnvelope construction. Authenticated metadata remains provenance, not proof of scene truth.

Considerations: never invent unsupported camera attestation; user-owned lab credentials remain capability-scoped; a single model score or two feeds sharing one failure domain are not independent corroboration.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover session binding, sequence windows, reconnect epochs, clock skew, duplicate/replay handling, key rotation/revocation, and shared-failure-domain math. Lab/E2E fixtures exercise cover, movement, dazzle, disconnect, jam, recorded-video replay, RTP reorder/loss, USB reconnect, stale cloud response, firmware drift, and partial custody. Outputs distinguish authenticated channel/device, suspected tamper, coverage loss, conflicted evidence, and unknown; false positives/negatives and costs are retained. Corroboration and negative reads require independent witnesses and CoverageWitness under the exact interval.

title: DOC-044 — Implement privacy-safe tracing, append-only audit, health telemetry, and bounded metrics
description:
Background: evidence, operational telemetry, and audit records have different semantics. The system needs detailed diagnosis and later accountability without turning logs, traces, metrics, prompts, or support bundles into a secret/protected-media side channel.

Approach: define stable event/error/span/metric identities and correlation through mission/session/workspace, request, Cx/region, subject, source session, EvidenceDeltaBatch, plan/effect/obligation and proof bundle. Append-only audit records authority/capability checks, secret access metadata, policy/config/model/device generation activation, reads/exports/deletes/effects, denials, repairs and release actions. Health telemetry reports queues, gaps, clock, storage, publication/replication, model/adapter status, resource pressure and degradation. Metrics use bounded-cardinality registered dimensions; high-cardinality detail uses protected handles. Apply privacy classification, redaction, retention and access transform before emission; raw frames/audio/secrets/tokens/prompts are prohibited.

Considerations: telemetry cannot upgrade evidence claims; audit failure follows fail-closed policy for consequential operations; tracing propagation carries identity, never ambient authority; sampling may not drop security/terminal/coverage transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Schema and policy tests prove registered IDs, bounded cardinality, correlation, ordering, rotation, retention, redaction, access control, tamper evidence, clock uncertainty, and fail-closed behavior. Adversarial tests inject secrets/protected content into errors, vendor fields, prompts and malformed payloads and verify exclusion. E2E fault scenarios reconstruct a cancellation, packet gap, archive partial, model crash, denied effect and indeterminate effect from audit/telemetry plus evidence handles while proving telemetry alone cannot claim success. Support bundles remain sanitized and reproducible.

title: DOC-045 — Secure signed updates, anti-rollback, provenance, staged activation, and revocation
description:
Background: immutable model/device/config generations and release artifacts are trust roots. Downloading “latest,” activating partial generations, or accepting older vulnerable state can silently change evidence and effect semantics.

Approach: define signed content-addressed manifests for binaries, crates/dependencies/SBOM, models/tokenizers/calibration, device compatibility data, schemas/registries/config/migrations and qualification receipts. Verify threshold/signing policy, trusted time/expiry, channel/profile/target, license, source revision and reproducible-build provenance before staging. Use root-last publication and atomic generation activation after compatibility, privacy, migration and rollback checks. Maintain monotonic anti-rollback counters with explicit emergency authorization, revocation lists and quarantine. Separate download/stage/visible/durable/active/protected/retrievable states. Never execute migration/vendor/lab code with ambient production secrets.

Considerations: offline update and recovery remain possible through signed bundles; rollback is to a still-authorized qualified generation; canary and lab are not stable authority; partial target matrices do not publish.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover manifest canonicalization/signature policy, expiry/time uncertainty, target/profile/channel matching, anti-rollback, revocation, dependency/SBOM completeness, and generation fencing. Fault E2E tests interrupt every stage, corrupt artifacts/manifests, replay old metadata, revoke active keys/models, fail migrations, exhaust storage, lose power and test rollback/uninstall. No partial root becomes active; current work either drains on its pinned generation or is explicitly invalidated. Release proof records immutable source/artifact hashes, complete target matrix, installer lifecycle, public verification and recovery instructions.

title: DOC-046 — Prove graph-complete deletion and distinguish cryptographic erasure from expiry and unknown copies
description:
Background: “deleted” is not one state. The plan distinguishes local logical/physical deletion, remote confirmed deletion, provider expiry scheduled/observed, cryptographic erasure, replica lag, legal hold, unreachable replica, and unknown third-party copies.

Approach: build a reachability graph from source and derivative evidence through indexes, embeddings, model/context caches, reports, bundles, ATP replicas, archives, backups, keys and audit-retained metadata. Prepare a witnessed deletion plan under current holds/authority; revalidate the graph root; execute idempotently; observe provider/replica outcomes; destroy/rotate isolated key material only when its reachability and sharing permit a valid cryptographic-erasure claim; rebuild/compact derived indexes; and publish a closure receipt enumerating terminal and outstanding nodes. Preserve minimal audit/proof metadata without retaining deleted content or claiming control over unknown copies.

Considerations: retention/hold changes are explicit policy generations; encryption-key deletion is not erasure if plaintext or another key remains; delayed provider expiry is an obligation; backups require tested closure or honest unknown.
acceptance_criteria: Graph/property tests detect every registered edge class, shared keys, cycles, new concurrent derivatives, holds, replica lag and unreachable/unknown nodes. E2E tests cover export then delete, cancel/resume, duplicate request, crash at every transition, offline archive, remote provider delay, key rotation, shared-key refusal, index rebuild and restored-backup non-resurrection. Receipts use typed per-node outcomes and never collapse partial/unknown into success. Privacy qualification verifies closure under each deployment profile and retention generation.

title: DOC-047 — Freeze exact operation, view, resource-URI, partial-success, refusal, and wait/watch semantics
description:
Background: all transports share the registered fss/1 semantic protocol. AgentSession, workspace, ContractBasis, envelopes, SituationFrame/WorldEnvelope, cases, affordances, plans, episodes and handoffs come from machine registries; CLI/MCP/TUI/report may not invent parallel nouns, success rules or low-level one-tool-per-command surfaces.

Approach: reconcile every AOP operation, AVIEW view and resource-template URI with request/response schemas, capabilities, costs, errors, hydration levels and recovery classes. Define per-operation read/write/effect authority, idempotency key, preconditions/witnesses, progressive/partial result contract, continuation/resnapshot, cancellation, expected decision fingerprint, effect obligation and terminal states. Define actionable refusal/unauthorized/not-observable/blocked/waiting/indeterminate responses with safe retry/rebase/reconcile/repair/approval/alternative guidance. Wait/watch is explicit, resumable and budgeted. Views are typed projections of one semantic root with compression receipts and privacy transforms.

Considerations: response envelopes never truncate mid-object; partial success names completed/remaining/invalidated work; follow streams never coalesce terminal, coverage loss, contradiction, urgent obligation or plan invalidation; recommendations never authorize commit.
acceptance_criteria: Registry audit reports exact one-to-one coverage of all operation IDs, view IDs, resource URI templates, error/recovery classes, capabilities and cost rows with no transport-only semantics. Golden transcript E2E tests prove Rust API/CLI/MCP/TUI/report equivalence, deterministic decision digests, idempotent retries, continuation, disconnect/resume, partial success, refusal guidance, wait/watch, approval and indeterminate reconciliation. Fuzz/fault tests reject malformed URIs/envelopes and stale anchors without performing effects or leaking redacted existence/count/rank.

title: DOC-048 — Qualify the Insta360 Link exact UVC/UAC tuple as the first native reference device
description:
Background: the plan names Insta360 Link as the first native standards-based reference camera while Wyze Cam v4 and AOSU P1 Max remain owner-authorized lab tuples. Compatibility attaches to an exact device/firmware/host/OS/adapter/config tuple, never a marketing family.

Approach: census USB descriptors, UVC modes/controls, UAC endpoints only if explicitly opted in, firmware and host-controller topology, OS/backend versions, pixel formats, frame rates/resolutions, timestamps, reconnect behavior, control quirks and bandwidth limits. Implement standards-first discovery/acquisition with explicit source-session epochs, Cx authority, bounded buffers, cancellation drain/finalize, source custody and health/coverage witnesses. Record unsupported controls honestly and quarantine tuple drift. Audio is hard-off by default and its absence is proved.

Considerations: app-only features are not native support; decoded frames without custody remain transient derivatives; firmware/USB topology drift expires the claim; device identity does not prove scene authenticity.

Claim activation requires QL-ADAPTER, QL-MEDIA, native platform and privacy proof; changed tuple is quarantined until requalification.

title: DOC-049 — Use bounded BOCPD regime monitors only for advisory workload and sensor adaptation
description:
Background: Bayesian online change-point detection may identify workload or sensor regimes, but adaptive policy is advisory and clamped. It may tune inspection depth, batch size, candidate count and path allocation; it may not weaken authority, freshness, coverage, integrity, privacy, retention or verification requirements, and it is not event evidence by itself.

Approach: implement a deterministic scalar BOCPD reference with fixed registered priors/hazard, bounded run-length state, canonical numeric policy, replay fixtures and explicit reset/generation semantics. Inputs are typed operational/sensor summaries with coverage and provenance; outputs are regime hypotheses with uncertainty, explanation, evidence window and expiration. Proposals pass hard clamps, resource budgets, hysteresis/cooldown and shadow evaluation before activation as a new advisory-policy generation. Preserve the prior complete generation and root-last activate; harmful proposals roll back and become negative evidence.

Considerations: clock gaps/reconnect/config changes are separate causes, model feedback may be correlated, privacy transformations precede monitoring, and a change point cannot prove intrusion/tamper.
acceptance_criteria: Reference/property tests cover priors, normalization, bounds, numeric stability, missing/gapped data, reset, replay, adversarial oscillation, false alarms and deterministic generation. Differential tests match the pinned FrankenSQLite oracle within registered tolerance. E2E pressure and sensor scenarios show allowed tuning improves full task quality/cost while clamps prevent safety/privacy/evidence degradation; missing coverage remains unknown. Every activation has a proposal, counterfactual baseline, cost/quality proof, generation receipt, expiry and rollback test.
