title: DOC-050 — Route internal work through typed semantic subjects with separate packet, authority, and reasoning service classes
description:
Background: FSS is a semantic subject fabric, not a tangle of channels or generic RPC. Internal work names a stable typed subject family and declared service class while packet movement, authority, and reasoning remain distinct planes.

Approach: register subject schemas for evidence deltas, custody/publication, graph/model work, agent cognition, plans/effects/obligations and proof. Compile routing from capability, privacy zone, data locality, resource pressure and deployment profile. A packet contains immutable objects/handles, provenance and budget; authority remains explicit Cx/capability and is never inferred from routing; reasoning results remain derived. Enforce bounded queues, region ownership, deadlines, priorities/fairness, backpressure, cancellation request→drain→finalize, lease/obligation accounting, and deterministic lab scheduling. ATP handles cross-process/host immutable object graphs; it never carries effect authority.

Considerations: packet-plane batching/reordering may not violate authority/freshness/terminal ordering; service classes cannot create a global lock or mutable singleton; subject versioning preserves tombstones and compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Registry/schema tests cover every subject/service class, capability compilation, privacy zone, version compatibility and forbidden cross-plane field. Property/fault tests prove bounded queues, fairness, backpressure, cancellation, region cleanup, retry/idempotency, stale generation, reordering and pressure degradation. E2E across deployment profiles proves identical semantic outcomes and explicit cost differences; packet optimization cannot relax authority, coverage, privacy or effect verification. Structured logs correlate subject, region, authority digest, budget, evidence roots and terminal disposition without carrying secrets.

title: DOC-051 — Model NVR/bridge provenance and battery/event-driven source coverage honestly
description:
Background: NVR and bridge integrations may be acquisition sources, but their streams can be direct, transcoded, delayed, composited or generated. Multiple cameras behind one NVR share a failure domain and NVR labels remain derived. Battery/event-driven cameras may sleep or expose only clips; they cannot be counted as continuous coverage.

Approach: extend exact adapter/source manifests with directness, transformation lineage, latency/clock behavior, multiplexing, upstream camera identity, NVR/base/cloud and power/network/account failure domains, and event-label provenance. For battery/solar sources record continuous/wake-on-motion/scheduled/import-only mode, pre/post-roll, wake latency, missed-event evidence, battery/solar state, cloud/base dependence, observable intervals and explicit between-event not_observable domains. Display/app bridges record lost packets/timestamps/metadata/resolution and may support temporary live/calibration/research without source-archive or continuity claims. Feed all duty cycles and shared failures into CoverageWitness, corroboration and WorldEnvelope.

Considerations: vendor/NVR metadata cannot enable privacy-sensitive features; app capture is exact-tuple lab work; source custody starts at the actual retained boundary; drift quarantines claims.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures and owner-authorized E2E tests cover direct/transcoded/delayed/composited NVR streams, multiple cameras behind one NVR, upstream outage, NVR clock drift/restart, sleeping/waking battery cameras, missed pre-roll, cloud/base outage, low battery, sparse clips and display capture. Outputs distinguish source/derivative custody, shared failure domains and observable gaps; negative reads fail without interval CoverageWitness. Compatibility certificates state exact tuple, duty cycle, limitations and invalidators, and QL-ADAPTER/THREAT proof never upgrades bridge or asleep-camera evidence.

title: DOC-052 — Choose remux, transcode, live delivery, archive tier, and backend portability with receipts
description:
Background: media movement is a decision-bearing physical policy. Remux before transcode preserves source-coded bytes and avoids quality/compute loss when compatible; transcode is justified only for compatibility, bitrate, privacy redaction or analysis and requires cost/quality lineage. Archive tiers and providers are placement, not semantic identity.

Approach: implement a deterministic Decision Card comparing passthrough/remux/transcode and live surfaces (authorized WebRTC, LL-HLS/CMAF/fMP4, same-host frame transport, justified RTP/RTSP relay) under codec/container/client, latency, bandwidth, privacy, CPU/GPU/energy, fidelity and custody constraints. Emit MediaDerivativeReceipt for every transform. Live gateway has no vendor credentials and receives capability-projected privacy-masked proxies with auth/bandwidth/expiry. Plan hot-local source, hot-remote event, standard historical, infrequent-access, metadata-after-expiry and hold archive tiers using dated storage/operation/retrieval/egress/duration/object-lock/region/durability measurements. Backend-neutral manifests preserve content/event identity; provider metadata/receipts are children and migration publishes new custody/location records without rewriting events.

Considerations: chunk sizing prices PUT/HEAD/GET/list/retry/deletion/seek/dedup/encryption; source is never silently transcoded or overwritten; unavailable codecs remain indexed/retained with explicit decode limits.

Goal naming: Archive portability means backend-neutral export, mirror, restore, and migration without semantic identity rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/differential tests prove byte-preserving remux, deterministic transform receipts, privacy-before-egress and correct live-session expiry. E2E scenarios compare remux/transcode/live choices, client incompatibility, cancellation, codec gap, bandwidth/thermal pressure, archive-tier transition, provider migration, egress/retrieval cost, legal hold, restore and backend removal. Every choice records source/derivative roots, fidelity, generations, full cost and invalidators. Exported roots reconstruct identically on another backend; no provider or live gateway changes canonical identity or gains vendor/effect authority.

title: DOC-053 — Calibrate coordinate frames with a safety-constrained shuttle, joint optimization, and effective coverage
description:
Background: the calibration shuttle links fixed-camera 2D observations to a mapped property using a manually piloted drone or handheld wand with a known marker/temporal code; static markers/known dimensions/common landmarks provide a weaker no-payload alternative. The twin is an inference and coverage instrument, not decorative 3D.

Approach: register directed timestamped/generation-bound property-world, camera optical/body/mount, drone body/camera/marker, map/floor/zone and optional GPS/ENU coordinate frames with covariance or conservative bounds. Joint optimization may estimate fixed intrinsics/extrinsics, drone trajectory, anchors, per-camera offset/drift, rolling shutter, scene surfaces, scale and robust outliers from deterministic initialization/order. Candidate classical/learned solvers publish certificates with exact code/config, residual/observability/held-out distributions and rejected status when gates fail. Shuttle planning enforces manual flight, owner authority, people/property safety, marker payload constraints and a no-payload fallback. Installed coverage is the accepted static certificate; effective versus installed coverage recomputes from live pose/settings/continuity/quality/privacy/daylight/weather/model health and is the only basis for event policy.

Considerations: transform cycles with large residual cannot activate; model confidence cannot bypass geometry/coverage; drift creates new evidence and shadow recalibration, never silent mutation.

Goal mapping: this is the calibrated sensor mesh contract, including geometry, time, effective coverage, uncertainty, and drift.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic-truth, held-out trajectory/marker, loop/cycle, crop/zoom/firmware/time drift, moved-camera, occlusion and no-payload tests pass with registered bounds. A controlled shuttle E2E retains mission/source roots, transforms, uncertainty, residuals, outliers, observability, scale, protected-volume lower bounds, blind spots, safety/authority and decision fingerprint. Live fault scenarios prove effective coverage degrades under obstruction, sleep, glare, privacy pause, model outage and drift while installed coverage remains historical; absence/corroboration conclusions follow the effective witness.

title: DOC-055 — Unify scenario taxonomy, split/statistical discipline, metamorphic tests, alert fatigue, red-team cadence, and incident response
description:
Background: threat correctness and operational safety require one evidence-bearing evaluation doctrine. Severity and urgency are distinct; alert fatigue is a safety/cost outcome; scenario taxonomy, split discipline, statistical method, metamorphic relations, red-team cadence and incident response cannot be scattered as informal test notes.

Approach: register normal/benign/threat/adversarial/failure/privacy/operations/agent scenarios with observable domain, tactic, environment, property/device/model/policy generations and shared failures. Prevent leakage with subject/property/device/time/firmware/event-family separation and sealed thresholds before held-out runs. Define denominators, uncertainty/confidence bounds, multiple slices, worst/high-loss results and raw-record retention; absence of samples is not zero. Metamorphic relations cover replay invariance, view/transport equivalence, monotone evidence, privacy/capability noninterference, duplication/reordering, time/geometry transformations and bounded degradation. Compute severity from potential harm/worlds and urgency from time-to-loss/obligation; policy handles rate/burst/dedup/escalation/suppression with explicit operator burden and never hides novel/contradictory/terminal signals. Conduct scheduled owner-authorized red-team exercises, preserve findings/negative evidence, and run incident response with containment, custody, communication, remediation, recovery and post-incident learning proposals without silent policy changes.

Considerations: percentages wait for sealed corpus/exposure denominator; red team never expands authority or attacks third parties; incident telemetry is not canonical evidence.

Goal mapping: this doctrine proves explainable event truth and crash and retry correctness under realistic statistical, adversarial, and operational conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests validate split leakage, statistical/percentile/confidence math, metamorphic oracles, severity/urgency separation and alert-budget state machines. Sealed E2E gauntlets cover benign hard negatives, staged intrusion/tamper/evasion, coverage gaps, duplicate storms, channel failure, operator fatigue and incident containment/recovery with detailed secret-free logs. Thresholds are fixed before holdout; raw per-slice results, false/true alerts/property-day, calibration, operator burden and costs are retained. Red-team and incident exercises yield evidence-linked findings/actions/expiry, and releases fail on unsafe slices, leakage, hidden suppression or missing response proof.

title: DOC-056 — Implement sealed ATP receipts, adaptive RaptorQ economics, and store-and-forward mailbox delivery
description:
Background: ATP transfers immutable verified object graphs, not effects. Receipt sealing distinguishes staged/visible/durable/replicated/protected/retrievable truth; adaptive RaptorQ and repair economics decide redundancy from loss/cost; store-and-forward mailbox semantics support disconnected or delayed destinations without inventing delivery success.

Approach: define manifest/offer/accept/path/journal/chunk/repair/reconstruction/verification/publication receipt state machines with root-last sealing and exact source/destination/capability/privacy identities. Adaptive RaptorQ selects repair symbol count from recorded path loss/correlation, object importance, latency, compute, bytes and provider cost under hard integrity floors; reconstruction always passes canonical digest. A mailbox stores encrypted capability-scoped immutable envelopes, deduplicates by content/idempotency, tracks custody and expiry, resumes journaled delivery, verifies receiver publication/retrievability and reports accepted/delivered/verified separately. Multiple paths race with loser drain and shared-failure-domain accounting. No transfer token grants commit/effect authority.

Considerations: offline, quota full, expired/revoked capability, corrupt shard, partial list, duplicate/reorder, receiver rollback and cancellation remain explicit obligations/indeterminate delivery states.
acceptance_criteria: State-machine/property/fault tests interrupt every ATP transition; cover duplicate/reorder/loss/corrupt repair, correlated paths, adaptive-versus-fixed redundancy cost, mailbox offline/expiry/quota/revocation, resume, receiver crash and loser drain. Receipt sealing publishes no root before complete closure and canonical verification; independent reconstruction matches the source root. Structured logs retain manifest/journal/repair/path/cost/timing/outcome digests without secrets. Archive/handoff/model delivery E2E distinguishes acceptance, durable mailbox custody, receiver publication and retrievability, and never claims effect completion.

title: DOC-057 — Keep adaptive learning, synthesized invariants, and speculative precomputation advisory and discardable
description:
Background: FrankenGraphDB research contributes three useful disciplines: Gradient means failures update engineering priors, not canonical truth; Mirror means invariants can be synthesized as proposals but promotion is reviewed; Wormhole means speculative precomputation is permitted only under strict discard rules. These do not create self-modifying policy.

Approach: convert failures/divergences/episodes into immutable evidence-linked feedback, learning or negative-evidence proposals with applicability, counterexamples, shared failures, harmful outcomes, decay/expiry and validation plan. Candidate invariants receive new proposed identities, formal/reference tests, counterexamples, proof cost and human/qualified promotion; they cannot rewrite active schemas/policy/authority. Speculative graph/search/model/context work runs on pinned branch anchors under separate budgets and capabilities; outputs remain invisible/advisory until the exact basis is still current and all semantic/privacy/cost gates pass. On mismatch, revocation, cancellation, pressure or objective change, drain and discard derived objects while retaining minimal cost/outcome evidence. Caches never become truth or effect authority.

Considerations: trauma guard prevents one harmful episode from overgeneralizing; beneficial learning is evaluated on held-out future tasks and can be demoted/revived; speculation cannot starve committed work or leak existence through timing/counts.
acceptance_criteria: Property/fault tests prove proposals cannot mutate active policy/invariants/capabilities, promotion requires explicit reviewed generation, and expired/harmful learning demotes without erasing history. Speculation tests cover anchor/policy/model/privacy drift, branch merge, cancellation, budget pressure, stale cache and adversarial timing; invalid work is unreachable/discarded and cannot affect decisions/effects. Held-out before/after E2E measures correctness, calibration, unsafe/evidence error, full resource/privacy/operator cost and transfer harm; every activation has proof, expiry, rollback and negative evidence.

description:

Doctor produces bounded typed repair plans and sanitized handles; it never auto-changes retention/privacy/authority/model policy. Pressure admission follows registered ladders: shed/rebuild derived work before source custody, preserve terminal/coverage/contradiction/effect uncertainty, and declare inability to retain/observe rather than overwrite or fabricate. Incident response links health to append-only audit and proof without treating telemetry as canonical scene evidence.

Considerations: overall status is a projection of dimensions with worst/high-loss visibility; role/privacy views cannot leak hidden resources; stale status says stale.

title: DOC-060 — Enforce the retention lattice across data class, subject, purpose, holds, replicas, and derived state
description:
Background: retention is a lattice, not a single duration. Effective policy combines data class and sensitivity, subject/context (owner, resident, guest, child, bystander), purpose/mission, evidence/incident status, consent and privacy transform, jurisdiction/operator rule, legal/insurance hold, storage/archive/replica class, export/share state and active obligation.

Approach: compute an immutable versioned RetentionDecision with contributing rules, meet/join precedence, start/expiry/uncertainty, allowed placements/transforms/access, hold overrides, derived-data ceiling, deletion/cryptographic-erasure plan and required proof. More permissive child/derived/cache/model/context/report policy cannot outlive or expose its source unless a separate authorized minimal record contract explicitly permits it. Policy changes apply prospectively or through witnessed migration; they never rewrite historical decision basis. Schedule expiration as durable obligations across local/remote/backup/provider nodes and expose lag/unknown honestly. Capability/privacy projection precedes queries, counts, export and hydration.

Considerations: holds preserve required data but do not expand readers/purpose; revocation may tighten future access; telemetry/audit retain only minimal allowed metadata; provider expiration is not immediate deletion.

Goal naming: the retention lattice is the ordered policy composition above, not a flat duration table.
acceptance_criteria: Lattice/property tests cover precedence, conflicting rules, child/bystander protection, consent/revocation, incident promotion, holds, derived/cache/report/model/context data, exports/replicas/backups, policy migration, clock uncertainty and immutable history. E2E advances virtual time through expiration, hold/release, provider delay, offline replica, cryptographic-erasure eligibility, restore and concurrent derivative creation. Every retained/deleted/lagging/unknown node has a typed reason and receipt; privacy qualification detects over-retention, under-retention required by hold, access expansion and resurrection.

title: Enforce the contributor workflow, architectural guardrails, qualification entrypoint and proof expectations
description:
Source-assimilation boundary:
Path: CONTRIBUTING.md
Role: This operational/reference document has its own status and authority boundary. # Contributing

FSS welcomes architecture review, standards expertise, device interoperability work on devices you
own or are authorized to test, Rust implementation, model evaluation, privacy review, red-team
fixtures, and operational testing.

## Before opening code

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, the comprehensive plan, `SECURITY.md`, and `PRIVACY.md`.
2. Identify the stable requirement, work package, gate, and readiness dimensions affected.
3. Check whether the change introduces a new dependency, authority, durable schema, model identity,
   effect class, secret path, privacy surface, or compatibility claim.
4. Add or update the relevant registry before relying on prose.
5. State what negative evidence would falsify the proposed approach.

## Hard rules

- No credential bypass, unauthorized access, covert deployment, or third-party footage.
- No committed credentials, tokens, device certificates, private packet captures, or household
  footage.
- No model or device support claim without an exact immutable identity and qualification artifact.
- No `unsafe` anywhere in the FSS workspace. A required low-level primitive must be implemented and qualified in an independently owned first-party substrate crate exposing a safe contract; FSS does not create local exceptions.
- No Tokio ecosystem in the workspace.
- No detached task. Production invokes no foreign subprocess; laboratory-oracle processes must be explicitly owned, bounded, drained, and excluded from release closure.
- No hidden network downloads during build or test.
- No mutable durable format serialized from an unversioned Rust enum.
- No benchmark result without raw samples, environment, oracle, variance, and reproduction command.
- No rewrite of canonical evidence by a cognition or memory component.

## Required local checks

```bash
bash scripts/qualify.sh
```

Device, model, archive, and performance changes add their own qualification lanes. Hosted CI is not
a substitute for the local proof bundle.

## Fixture policy

Fixtures must be synthetic, public-domain, or explicitly consented. Include a provenance manifest,
consent class, deletion owner, expected observations, expected non-observations, and known limits.
Sanitize packet captures so they contain no credentials, unique device secrets, account IDs,
private network names, faces, license plates, addresses, or unrelated audio.

## Commit discipline

Prefer small semantic commits whose message names the stable work item. Documentation, schemas,
registries, implementation, tests, and status must move together. A feature is not complete merely
because its happy-path code exists.

# Negative evidence ledger

This ledger records hypotheses that failed, did not improve the system, or produced a narrower
result than expected. A failed experiment is not deleted when a new candidate appears.

## Required fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ID | Stable `NEG-###` identifier |
| Date / commit | Exact experiment context |
| Hypothesis | What was expected and why |
| Setup | Corpus, device/model/firmware/platform, policy, command, and artifact digests |
| Result | Measurements, failures, divergences, and confidence |
| Decision | Reject, retain as oracle, narrow scope, or revisit |
| Revival condition | New evidence that would justify repeating the work |

## Entries

No implementation experiments have been run. The architecture research already records these
negative constraints:

### NEG-001 — Do not make DJI Flip SDK support an architectural dependency

- **Hypothesis:** the drone can be treated as a normal officially supported DJI Mobile SDK source.
- **Finding:** current public supported-product documentation does not establish DJI Flip support.
- **Decision:** recorded-file import and authorized capture-bridge experiments only; manual flight;
  an unsupported result is acceptable.
- **Revival:** an official compatible SDK/product listing or a repeatable, owner-authorized,
  supportable capture surface.

### NEG-002 — Do not treat proprietary app access as a stable camera standard

- **Hypothesis:** a consumer camera advertised with Wi-Fi/cloud viewing has a stable local stream.
- **Finding:** public owner-facing documentation for target proprietary products does not establish
  a durable ONVIF/RTSP contract.
- **Decision:** standards-first adapters; vendor paths remain exact-tuple interoperability-lab work.
- **Revival:** official local API/profile support or a qualified owner-authorized adapter matrix.

### NEG-003 — Do not select one frontier VLM as the complete security stack

- **Hypothesis:** the newest large multimodal model can replace detection, tracking, geometry, and
  calibrated event policy.
- **Finding:** latency, licensing, temporal grounding, reproducibility, and failure isolation differ
  by task; no single current candidate establishes the complete contract.
- **Decision:** progressive model cascade with immutable generations and held-out event gauntlets.
- **Revival:** a candidate passes every task, license, cost, privacy, and deterministic boundary
  against the decomposed incumbent under the same workload.

# Object-storage pricing reference — 2026-08-30

This is a dated research input, not executable configuration. Re-check provider documentation
before implementation, deployment, or a cost claim.

## Cloudflare R2

The official pricing page consulted for this design lists Standard storage at **$0.015 per GB-month**,
Class A operations at **$4.50 per million**, Class B operations at **$0.36 per million**, and no
Internet egress charge from R2 itself, subject to the provider's current definitions and free tier.
R2 exposes an S3-compatible API with documented differences.

## Backblaze B2

The official pricing material consulted for this design lists pay-as-you-go storage at
**$6.95 per TB-month**, with free egress up to three times average monthly stored data and additional
provider/partner terms that must be evaluated for the actual access pattern.

## FSS rule

Provider prices, request classes, minimum-storage rules, retrieval/egress policies, and effective
dates belong in a signed runtime pricing manifest. The archive planner reports storage, request,
retrieval/egress, and local-compute costs separately. This document must never be imported as a
permanent constant.

See [`REFERENCES.md`](REFERENCES.md) for official source URLs.


Operationalization requirements:
1. Treat machine registries/schemas as higher authority, but record and repair any disagreement rather than choosing convenient text.
2. Preserve stable identities, assumptions, alternatives, failure/unknown states, privacy/security limits, costs, qualification and claim boundaries.
3. Add deterministic source-digest and heading/row coverage checks with typed drift diagnostics and owner/repair guidance.
4. Update the bead and its dependent proof whenever the source is deliberately changed; generated prose must remain a mirror, not a parallel contract.

title: DOC-008 — Implement privacy data classes, minimization, and retention policy
description:
Outcome
Encode P0-P3 or registered data classes, purpose, owner, consent basis, access transform, storage locations, TTL, holds, derived-object propagation, and deletion eligibility. Default to local minimization and explicit audio/remote-transfer denial.

Background and intent
Privacy is a cross-cutting coordinate on every object and view, not a late UI filter.

Contract constraints
Use registered stable identities and versioned schemas; preserve authority, knowledge state, provenance, hypothesis disposition, effect outcome, uncertainty, contradictions, coverage, redaction, and generation validity as orthogonal fields. All I/O/time/effects require explicit authority; publication is root-last; derived state is rebuildable from EvidenceDeltaBatch history. Failure must be typed and actionable, never null or silent fallback.

Verification
Add deterministic reference and unit tests for success, bounds, malformed input, stale generation, unauthorized access, duplicate requests, cancellation drain, crash/restart, migration, and privacy transforms. Add an end-to-end script through the canonical CLI or registered transport with structured JSON logs containing scenario/step/operation IDs, seeds, virtual or interval time, authority and anchor digests, input/output/evidence digests, exact generations, budget/cost deltas, expected and actual outcome, cleanup and obligation state, and retained artifact links. Exercise resource pressure and prove diagnostics contain no secrets or raw sensitive bytes.

Exact v1 data-class taxonomy:
- P0 Operational: camera health, firmware tuple and queue depth; long retention, low privacy sensitivity.
- P1 Environmental: weather, illumination and anonymous motion heatmaps; utility-scoped retention without identity reconstruction.
- P2 Resident-sensitive: routines, recognizable people and interiors; local encrypted storage, short ordinary retention and strict export.
- P3 Highly sensitive: audio, faces, license plates, access codes and children’s areas; disabled/minimized by default with explicit opt-in and policy.
- P4 Incident evidence: confirmed/suspected intrusion bundle; explicit legal/operational retention, immutable audit and redaction variants.
- P5 Secrets: passwords, tokens, cookies and private keys; secret-store handles only, never normal media/ledger payload.
One capsule may contain different classes by region/channel. Privacy transforms create new lineage-linked objects and never overwrite source truth. Every object gets a machine-evaluable retention reason and all derived forms—embeddings, tracks, thumbnails, captions, prompts/outputs, indexes, caches, transcripts, backups and remote mirrors—inherit deletion/retention constraints.

The complete outcome is represented in registries/schemas and documented without parallel vocabulary; deterministic unit, differential where applicable, fault, privacy/security, migration, cancellation, and resource-economy tests pass; the end-to-end script is repeatable from a clean controlled snapshot with detailed structured logs and explicit failure assertions; proof artifacts and exact generations are retained; unsupported/degraded cases and safe repair guidance are exposed; status and public claims do not exceed evidence.
- The exact P0 Operational, P1 Environmental, P2 Resident-sensitive, P3 Highly sensitive, P4 Incident evidence and P5 Secrets classes, defaults and allowed transforms are encoded and migration-tested.
- Mixed-class region/channel data, lineage-preserving minimization, derived-data propagation and secret-handle exclusion are tested end to end.

title: Define and prove the cross-adapter acquisition lifecycle
description:
## Outcome
Define one adapter-neutral acquisition state machine used by UVC, RTSP/RTP/ONVIF, replay/import, and authorized proprietary laboratory adapters: Requested → Authenticated → AdapterAccepted → FirstFrameObserved → ContinuityVerified, with explicit Degraded, Failed, Cancelled, and Indeterminate branches. Stream acceptance is never called streaming, a decoded frame is not continuity, and semantic detection is outside this state machine.

## Witness contract
Requested binds the canonical request digest and capability scope. Authenticated requires a secret-free AuthReceipt. AdapterAccepted requires the adapter ACK and exact request digest. FirstFrameObserved requires a bounded decodable frame linked to source bytes or an explicit source-retention omission. ContinuityVerified requires a declared window with packet/frame sequence, timing intervals, discontinuities, gap/jitter thresholds, and CoverageWitness. Degraded names lost dimensions and invalidated negative claims. Stop requires a quiescence receipt. Reconnect always creates a new stream generation; sequence reset cannot silently continue the old generation. No transition is inferred from elapsed time alone.

## Proof, failure, and observability contract
Use a deterministic safe-Rust reference first. Preserve stable identities, exact ContractBasis/EvidenceAnchor and generation inputs, capability/privacy projection, typed unknown/redacted/stale/conflicted/indeterminate outcomes, bounded resources, and request→drain→finalize cancellation. Unit and property tests cover every transition and invariant. Fault tests cover malformed inputs, duplicates/reordering, stale anchors/generations, cancellation at every boundary, crash/restart, partial I/O, pressure, authority/privacy revocation, and incompatible versions. A realistic end-to-end script must exercise success plus safe failure through the public semantic surface and retain secret-free structured logs with scenario/seed, fixture/source root, authority/privacy, transition sequence, injected schedule/fault, budgets/observed work, outcome/error identity, decision/output digests, proof handles, cleanup/obligation state, and an exact reproduction command. No log may contain raw private media, credentials, or unbounded payloads.
acceptance_criteria:
- A versioned typed transition table defines allowed predecessors, witness schema, terminality, retry class, and invalidators for every state/branch.
- All adapters expose the same lifecycle vocabulary without transport-specific aliases that collapse acceptance, first frame, or continuity.
- Tests reject skipped/reordered/duplicate transitions, forged or stale witnesses, reconnect generation reuse, timeout-only success, and continuity across a gap.
- E2e fixtures cover clean startup, accepted/no-frame, first-frame/no-continuity, degradation/recovery, cancellation, reconnect, and indeterminate stop with detailed transition logs.
- Coverage-dependent consumers cannot claim absence until ContinuityVerified plus a valid CoverageWitness.

title: Make CLI argument decoding total and reject trailing arguments deterministically
description:
## Finding and impact

The current command skeleton reads std::env::args and accepts known zero-argument commands without proving end-of-input. As a result, commands such as fss status --json extra, fss doctor --json extra, and fss capabilities --json extra can report success while silently ignoring malformed trailing input. The Unicode-only iterator can also panic before the registered error contract is reached when an operating-system argument is not valid UTF-8.

This is an agent API correctness defect. Silent argument acceptance makes typos and version skew look successful, undermines stable automation, and can cause an agent to believe an option was honored when it was discarded. A panic bypasses AgentResponseEnvelope, stable exit identity, redacted diagnostics, and continuation guidance.

## Required implementation contract

- Parse from OS-native arguments such as OsString and make conversion failure an explicit typed CLI error; no panic or lossy implicit conversion.
- Define each subcommand from the machine-readable command/field registry and require exact exhaustion of its grammar. A zero-argument command must reject every trailing token.
- Distinguish unknown command, unknown option, missing value, duplicate mutually exclusive option, malformed value, invalid Unicode, unexpected positional argument, and trailing argument with stable error and exit identities.
- Preserve the intended global versus subcommand option ordering explicitly. If both placements are supported, test and register both; otherwise reject the unsupported form rather than ignoring it.
- Keep stdout machine-clean: successful JSON/envelope output only. Diagnostics and human guidance go to stderr, and failure output follows the registered envelope/exit contract.
- Include safe repair guidance such as corrected usage, supported fields, retryability, and whether any effect could have begun. Parsing failures must occur before effects, leases, budget consumption, or workspace mutation.
- Generate or validate help/usage from the same registry so parser, documentation, schemas, and compatibility aliases cannot drift.
- Bound input length and diagnostic rendering. Never echo secrets or an entire hostile argument; use redacted/truncated representations and argument indexes.
- Retain deterministic behavior across Unix byte arguments and supported Windows wide-string semantics.

## Failure and compatibility considerations

Do not preserve accidental acceptance of ignored arguments as compatibility. If existing callers depended on it, expose the break through the compatibility registry and migration guidance. Alias removal and deprecation must follow the stable-ID/tombstone policy.

The parser and test helpers remain unsafe-free. Any asynchronous command path begins only after parsing and validation establish a complete typed request and explicit authority.

## Required proof

Table-driven unit tests cover every registered command, valid option ordering, exhaustion, missing and duplicate values, unknown command/option, unexpected positionals, trailing tokens, empty tokens, option-like values, non-UTF8 Unix arguments, bounded long inputs, and help/version behavior. Property or fuzz tests assert totality, no panic, deterministic parse results, bounded error size, and that adding an unregistered token cannot preserve success. Golden tests pin exit code, stdout bytes, stderr/error envelope, stable error ID, usage digest, and redaction.

A real-process end-to-end script must invoke the built binary for successful human and JSON modes and every failure class, including the three currently permissive command examples. It must prove nonzero stable exits, empty or schema-valid stdout as appropriate, diagnostic stderr, zero effects and authority changes, and retained proof artifacts. Structured logs must include command identity when known, parser phase, argument index and redacted class, stable error/exit IDs, registry and ContractBasis versions, correlation ID, effect-started false, and proof-bundle handle.
acceptance_criteria: Every command parses OS-native arguments without panic, consumes exactly its registered grammar, rejects trailing or malformed input with stable exit/error identities, preserves stdout/stderr and envelope contracts, and has unit, property/fuzz, compatibility, and real-process e2e proof with redacted diagnostic logging.

Therefore additional trailing tokens are silently accepted, while non-Unicode OS arguments may panic before the registered error surface. The bead requires a total OS-native parser, exact grammar exhaustion, pre-effect failure, and real-process proof.

title: Close Cargo policy blind spots across conditional dependencies and every Rust target
description:
## Fresh-eyes finding and risk

The current policy gate audits a strict subset of Cargo's semantic surface.

In scripts/dependency_audit.py, direct_dependency_rows reads only top-level dependencies, dev-dependencies, build-dependencies, and root workspace.dependencies. scripts/check-policy.py repeats the same top-level assumption. Neither walks target-specific tables such as target cfg dependencies, target dev-dependencies, or target build-dependencies. An unallowlisted or forbidden dependency can therefore be hidden behind a platform predicate; a target-specific build dependency can evade the explicit ban. The resolved-package audit does not close the hole because it checks only forbidden names, custom-build targets, native links, and unresolved Git sources—not the full allowlist, features, admission record, or every supported-target activation.

Target-root discovery is also incomplete. Both scripts inspect src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, and explicitly declared bin/example/test/bench paths. They omit Cargo auto-discovered src/bin targets, examples, integration tests, benches, build.rs, nested/glob workspace members, and auto-target enable/disable semantics. A future target can therefore lack the required local #![forbid(unsafe_code)] declaration while policy still passes. Path dependencies inside the repository are exempted from name/admission checks, allowing an undeclared non-member crate to enter production closure.

This is a false-green constitutional gate, not a cosmetic linter enhancement. The dependency and unsafe rules are production security and release-authority boundaries.

## Required implementation contract

- Derive the workspace/package/target/dependency graph from Cargo semantics under the pinned nightly and locked offline resolution, while retaining a small deterministic parser/reference oracle that can detect tool-output drift.
- Expand workspace globs and exclusions exactly, reject duplicate/ambiguous membership, and bind every package to crate topology, owner, import/admission record, license, source identity, features, target predicate, and status.
- Enumerate normal, dev, and build dependencies at package, workspace-inherited, and every target-specific table. Validate table and field types before iterating them.
- Evaluate activation for every required release/qualification target and also retain dormant conditional rows so a dependency cannot hide merely because the current host does not select it.
- Treat renamed packages by package identity while preserving the local alias in diagnostics. Resolve workspace = true inheritance and validate the effective source, version/revision, default features, features, optionality, and target condition.
- Require every path dependency to resolve within an explicitly registered repository or exact sibling closure, name a known workspace/import owner, and pass the same topology, unsafe, license, feature, and admission gates. Symlink, case-folding, traversal, and time-of-check/time-of-use escapes fail closed.
- Discover every Cargo target: lib/proc-macro, primary and src/bin binaries, examples, integration tests, benches, explicitly declared targets, build.rs/custom-build helpers, and future supported target kinds. Honor autobins/autoexamples/autotests/autobenches and custom paths.
- Require #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in every FSS crate/target/example/test/build helper exactly as the constitution states. Workspace lint inheritance is additional defense, not a substitute for the local declaration.
- Detect native links, custom build, foreign runtime, second executor, dynamic loading, prohibited command, runtime acquisition, and forbidden dependency/feature patterns across the complete source and resolved graph.
- Assign stable typed findings for newly distinguished cases and reconcile them with the canonical error registry; do not overload one diagnostic so heavily that repair guidance becomes ambiguous.
- Produce stable-order, content-addressed JSON output that records manifest/package/target/table/predicate/source/features/admission/generation and exact failure, without emitting credentials, source contents, or ambient environment secrets.
- Keep the check usable offline from a clean snapshot. Missing target metadata, unsupported cfg evaluation, unavailable pinned toolchain, or partial target matrix is a typed non-pass, never permission to scan less.

## Failure and compatibility considerations

Existing green results cover only the prior audit surface and must not be presented as proof of the expanded contract. Version the audit schema and finding identities, preserve older diagnostics through mappings/tombstones, and state which historical receipts are invalidated. Do not silently grandfather path crates, build helpers, target tables, or implicit auto targets.

The implementation must remain deterministic, bounded, unsafe-free, and compatible with local DSR release authority. Hosted jobs may exercise it but cannot substitute a partial host target.

## Required proof and logging

Unit and table-driven tests cover all dependency sections, target cfg expressions, renamed dependencies, workspace inheritance, optional/default/explicit features, malformed TOML types, exact and inexact Git revisions, allowlisted/unallowlisted/forbidden packages, registered and rogue path crates, sibling closure, traversal/symlink/case escapes, workspace globs/excludes, and every auto/explicit target kind. Property tests generate Cargo manifests and assert that adding a semantically reachable dependency or target cannot reduce the census or preserve a qualifying result when it violates policy.

Differential tests compare the deterministic reference census with pinned cargo metadata for every required target. Fault tests cover missing toolchain/lockfile/member, corrupt metadata, stale snapshots, conditional rows unselected on the host, concurrent manifest changes, output bounds, cancellation, and partial target matrices.

A real clean-snapshot end-to-end script must introduce each bypass class into fixtures, execute both policy entrypoints directly and through QL-POLICY-001 on the supported target matrix, and prove stable failure, no qualifying root, and exact repair guidance. The valid fixture must produce semantically identical censuses across repeated runs. Structured logs include audit/schema version, source/tree/lock/toolchain/target digests, package/manifest/target/table/predicate IDs, effective source and feature digest, admission/topology owner, finding/error ID, expected/actual outcome, matrix completeness, costs, artifact hashes, and proof root; they never include credentials or source payloads.
acceptance_criteria: The policy and dependency-audit entrypoints enumerate the exact Cargo workspace, every dependency table and resolved feature/source for every supported target, and every explicit or auto-discovered Rust/build target; no conditional, renamed, workspace-inherited, path, nested, glob, or build-script surface can bypass allowlist/admission or forbid-unsafe rules; deterministic unit/property/fault and cross-target e2e proof emits stable redacted diagnostics.

They do not walk target cfg dependency tables or Cargo auto-discovered targets/build.rs; path dependencies also bypass admission/name checks at dependency_audit.py:153-156 and check-policy.py:261-266. This bead closes the full Cargo semantic surface and requires multi-target proof.

title: Make Draft 2020-12 schema meta-validation mandatory, offline, and reproducible
description:
## Fresh-eyes finding and risk

scripts/check-policy.py currently performs Draft 2020-12 meta-schema validation only when an ambient Python jsonschema package happens to be importable. When it is absent, the script appends a note, still reports policy check passed, and returns success. The current repository environment demonstrates that exact path: the check passes while stating that meta-schema validation was skipped.

JSON Schemas are first-tier authoritative contracts in the repository truth hierarchy. A policy result that depends on an undeclared ambient package and treats its absence as success is neither deterministic nor fail-closed. The existing shallow checks—JSON parsing, top-level object/type conventions, selected required fields, and local $ref pointer existence—cannot establish that keyword values, regular expressions, vocabularies, combinators, anchors, numeric/string bounds, formats chosen as normative, or dialect semantics are valid. A malformed schema can therefore remain authoritative-looking and enter generated code, envelopes, compatibility decisions, proof receipts, or release claims.

## Required implementation contract

- Make complete schema meta-validation an unconditional part of the repository-local policy and qualification contract. Absence, version drift, unsupported vocabulary/dialect, or incomplete validation is a typed non-pass.
- Use a first-party pure-Rust validator or another dependency explicitly admitted, pinned, licensed, locked, offline-provisioned, and included in exact source/sibling closure. Do not rely on whichever Python package is installed on a host.
- Freeze the supported JSON Schema dialect and vocabularies. Draft 2020-12 core/applicator/validation/meta-data/format-annotation/content/unevaluated behavior and any deliberate exclusions must be explicit and testable.
- Validate every schema against the exact retained meta-schemas and validate the catalog as a graph, including $id, $schema, $ref, $dynamicRef, anchors, dynamic anchors, JSON Pointer decoding, URI normalization, fragments, cross-file cycles, recursion, and duplicate canonical identities.
- Resolve repository-local references within the registered schema root only. Network fetches, mutable remote resolution, path traversal, symlink escape, URI aliasing, and case-fold collisions fail closed.
- Separate meta-schema validity from instance conformance. The policy lane proves that schemas are well-formed and resolvable; each owning schema bead still provides positive/negative instance fixtures and semantic invariants.
- Establish stable typed diagnostics for invalid dialect, vocabulary, keyword shape, regex, URI/reference, anchor, pointer, recursion/resource limit, duplicate identity, unavailable validator, and incomplete catalog.
- Bound recursion, graph expansion, regex compilation/execution, input bytes, diagnostic size, and number of reported failures without truncating mid-object. Return continuation/proof handles for a bounded report.
- Canonicalize validation order and result serialization. The same source catalog and validator generation must yield identical finding order, digests, and exit identity across qualified hosts.
- Record validator implementation/version/digest and meta-schema catalog digest in ContractBasis and qualification receipts. A change invalidates prior compatibility proof until migrated and requalified.
- Preserve privacy and secret boundaries: schemas and diagnostics must not cause arbitrary external file reads or echo hostile instance/source content.

## Failure and compatibility considerations

The former pass-with-note behavior is historical partial evidence only. It may still be useful as a shallow source audit, but it cannot qualify the schema constitution or any gate that depends on it. Version the policy receipt and claim boundary so old results cannot be mistaken for the stronger proof.

Do not solve this by adding an unpinned network-installed Python dependency or by weakening the closed dependency universe. If a bootstrap validator is used, its source, meta-schemas, licenses, and build path are part of the immutable release closure and must qualify themselves against sealed fixtures and an independent oracle.

## Required proof and logging

Unit tests cover every supported keyword value type, all local reference forms, escaped JSON Pointers, IDs/anchors/dynamic anchors, recursive and mutually recursive schemas, duplicate IDs, missing targets, invalid regex, contradictory or malformed bounds, unsupported dialect/vocabulary, canonical ordering, and all resource limits. Negative fixtures include path/URI/symlink escape, network URLs, alias cycles, deep recursion, reference bombs, enormous diagnostics, invalid UTF-8 at file boundaries, and schema changes during validation.

Property tests generate bounded schema graphs and assert totality, deterministic results, graph-closure preservation, and that removing or corrupting a referenced contract cannot preserve qualification. Differential tests compare the production validator with at least one sealed independent Draft 2020-12 oracle over valid and invalid corpora; disagreements remain typed non-pass evidence and never select the convenient answer.

A direct end-to-end script must execute the policy and QL-POLICY-001 paths in a clean environment with no ambient jsonschema package, prove that the valid catalog qualifies, then inject each malformed/reference/resource class and prove stable failure with no qualifying root. It must also prove that adding an unrelated ambient package cannot change bytes or status. Structured logs include validator/meta-schema/catalog/source digests, schema stable ID and bounded path, dialect/vocabulary, reference/anchor/pointer identity, scenario and seed, expected/actual typed result, resource counters, disagreement/continuation/proof handles, exit ID, and artifact hashes; no schema instance secrets or hostile bulk bytes are logged.
acceptance_criteria: The authoritative policy lane always performs complete deterministic Draft 2020-12 meta-schema and local-reference validation from the locked offline source closure; validator absence or partial dialect support is a typed non-pass; malformed, adversarial, cyclic, and valid fixtures have unit/property/differential/e2e proof and stable bounded logs.

This bead converts that environment-dependent false green into an offline deterministic mandatory gate.

title: Pin every hosted workflow action to reviewed immutable provenance
description:
## Fresh-eyes finding and threat boundary

Both hosted workflow specifications invoke actions/checkout through the mutable symbolic reference actions/checkout@v4. Seven jobs currently use that form. The workflows run on self-hosted FSS runners, so the action executes before repository-owned qualification logic. A changed or compromised upstream tag can therefore execute with runner/network/repository context even though hosted results are explicitly supplementary and cannot publish the authoritative release root.

The current workflow policy checks delegation and rejects some duplicated setup logic, but it does not reject floating action references or bind actions to an admission/provenance record. Local DSR release authority limits claim damage; it does not make arbitrary code execution on a self-hosted runner acceptable.

## Required implementation contract

- Replace every external action reference with an exact full commit digest. Keep the human-readable release name in a comment or generated projection, not as executable identity.
- Register each action owner/repository/commit, source URL, release/tag mapping, license, security review, permissions, inputs, expected outputs, network behavior, update owner, expiry/review cadence, and approved workflow/job scope.
- Add a deterministic workflow policy that parses YAML structurally and rejects tags, branches, short SHAs, expressions that produce action identities, unregistered local/remote actions, Docker references without immutable digest, reusable workflows without exact commit, and action aliases whose owner/repository/commit do not match the allowlist.
- Do not rely on text fragments alone. Resolve anchors, aliases, reusable-workflow calls, nested composite actions, case/Unicode/whitespace variants, and every supported workflow extension without executing the workflow.
- Minimize token/job permissions and pin the runner image/profile separately. Checkout credentials must not persist beyond need; untrusted pull-request code must not obtain secrets or a privileged self-hosted execution path.
- Record the action closure in repository/source manifests and policy receipts. A pin change is a reviewed dependency update with new provenance and invalidates prior workflow-supply-chain proof.
- Preserve the architectural boundary: workflows remain portable supplementary specifications. A pin or green workflow never becomes local DSR release authority and cannot introduce unique qualification or publication logic.
- Treat unavailable upstream provenance, revoked/rewritten source, license change, nested mutable dependency, missing runner isolation, or partial action census as a typed non-pass with safe remediation.
- Keep diagnostics bounded and secret-free; do not print tokens, checkout credentials, environment secrets, or full hostile workflow content.

## Failure, migration, and update considerations

The initial pin must be selected from the upstream source corresponding to the intended reviewed checkout release, with verification independent of the mutable tag. Future automation may propose pin updates and attach diffs/advisories, but may not merge or activate them automatically. Preserve superseded pins and review outcomes as historical provenance.

If hosted workflow use is suspended, represent it as unavailable/disabled supplementary execution rather than falling back to a floating reference. Local direct/DSR qualification remains usable.

## Required proof and logging

Unit tests cover full and short SHAs, tags, branches, owner/repository spoofing, uppercase hex, YAML anchors/aliases, quoted/unquoted uses values, reusable workflows, local/composite actions, Docker digests, expression injection, malformed YAML, duplicates, permission escalation, persist-credentials, pull-request trust boundaries, and unregistered nested actions. Property tests generate workflow shapes and assert that replacing an immutable reference with a mutable or unknown identity cannot preserve a pass.

A repository-level end-to-end fixture must run the structural policy against the real workflow set, prove the exact seven former floating references are eliminated, and inject each bypass class into sealed fixture workflows. A controlled supplementary runner rehearsal verifies checkout and repository qualifier behavior using the pinned closure, no release publication capability, and no secret exposure. Structured logs include workflow/job/step IDs, action owner/repository/commit digest, admission and license record, permissions/trust class, source/workflow/policy digests, expected/actual typed finding, update review identity, runner profile, exit status, and proof root without credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Every external workflow action is allowlisted and pinned to an exact reviewed commit digest with source/license/provenance and controlled update semantics; symbolic tags and mutable refs fail policy before runner execution where possible; unit/property and workflow-fixture e2e tests retain stable redacted logs and prove supplementary workflows cannot upgrade release authority.

title: Bug: make the stable-ID census definition-aware and exhaustive across namespace widths
description:
## Observed false green
The current scripts/check-policy.py stable-ID census uses a hard-coded regex limited to selected namespaces ending in exactly three digits, inserts matches into a set, and reports only the resulting unique count. It therefore omits the variable-width North Star NS-1 through NS-13 family, cannot distinguish a definition from an ordinary reference, and silently collapses repeated definitions. The current policy check passes and reports 1,076 unique IDs even though the normative plan contains conflicting duplicate GOAL-019/020 definitions and duplicate NS-9/10 scenario definitions. Passing parse/link/registry checks is useful but is not complete identity validation.

## Required implementation
Define the stable-ID namespace grammar and allowed numeric width/status in a versioned machine contract rather than another ad hoc regex. Enumerate every normative family, including IDs with four digits or variable-width legacy forms, and classify each occurrence as definition, reference, alias, successor, tombstone, example, or malformed near-match. A definition has a semantic fingerprint over its owning source/row and cannot be deduplicated before collision analysis. References must resolve to exactly one active owner or an explicit historical mapping. Unknown namespaces and newly introduced families fail with an owned extension path rather than disappearing from totals.

## Scope and compatibility
Integrate the parser with the architecture/registry consistency checker, source snapshot, mirror generator, claim/proof checker, GATE-000 declaration validator, and generated traceability. Preserve historical IDs and source line/digest provenance. Namespace grammar changes require versioning, migration, affected-proof invalidation, and claim review. The checker remains read-only and deterministic under concurrent source mutation: it either validates one exact snapshot or returns a typed resnapshot-required result.

## Tests, E2E, and logs
Unit/golden/property fixtures cover every registered namespace and width; NS-1 and NS-10; ADR-0001; hierarchical IDs; exact duplicate definitions; conflicting duplicate meanings; repeated references; aliases/tombstones; missing owners; dangling references; malformed case/zero padding; ID-like prose/code examples; Unicode boundaries; CRLF/BOM; and source mutation during scan. The repository E2E must reproduce the current false green, then prove the corrected checker reports the GOAL and NS conflicts until DRIFT-001/002 repair them. Emit bounded secret-free JSONL with grammar version, source path/digest/line/span, occurrence kind, ID, semantic fingerprint, owner/status, resolution, per-family definition/reference/tombstone counts, diagnostic/repair, snapshot root, cost, and exact reproduction command.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned machine grammar exhaustively covers every normative stable-ID family and legal width, explicitly including NS-1 through NS-13 and ADR-0001-style identities. The checker classifies occurrences before counting, never uses set deduplication to hide multiple definitions, resolves every reference to one active owner or historical mapping, and rejects unknown families, conflicting definitions, dangling aliases/references, malformed forms, and snapshot races with stable diagnostics. Unit/golden/property tests cover every named boundary and the exact GOAL-019/020 plus NS-9/10 regressions. A direct local policy E2E demonstrates that the old corpus is no longer a false green, retains structured logs and a content-addressed proof root, and only GATE-000-compatible reconciled input passes.

Make the normative runtime tree an executable ownership contract: ProcessRegion owns PropertyRegion; PropertyRegion owns LedgerRegion, ObjectStoreRegion, ProjectionRegion, zero or more SensorRegions, zero or more EventRegions, and OperationsRegion. Each SensorRegion owns AdapterSessionRegion, ReceiveRegion, ContinuityRegion, MediaRegion, AnalysisRegion, and ArchiveRegion. Each EventRegion owns EvidenceWindowRegion, zero or more ModelCallRegions, AssociationRegion, PolicyRegion, and AlertObligationRegion.

## Semantics
Every child has exactly one owner. Cx authority reaches all I/O, time, sleep, lock, network, secret, effect, and sealed laboratory-process boundaries. Context cloning preserves or narrows trace/operation/principal/capability, deadlines, priority, cancellation reason, poll/byte/frame/token/model/GPU/object/memory budgets, privacy/retention scope, anchor universe, lease/fence/idempotency, and deterministic laboratory controls; it never broadens authority. Closure is request→drain→finalize and cannot report success while any descendant, callback, provider attempt, staged publication, lease, temporary object, or cleanup obligation remains live. A non-resolvable external effect becomes typed Indeterminate with a durable reconciliation obligation, not an orphan task or false failure/success.

## Proof, failure, and observability contract
Use a deterministic safe-Rust reference first. Preserve stable identities, exact ContractBasis/EvidenceAnchor and generation inputs, capability/privacy projection, typed unknown/redacted/stale/conflicted/indeterminate outcomes, bounded resources, and request→drain→finalize cancellation. Unit and property tests cover every transition and invariant. Fault tests cover malformed inputs, duplicates/reordering, stale anchors/generations, cancellation at every boundary, crash/restart, partial I/O, pressure, authority/privacy revocation, and incompatible versions. A realistic end-to-end script must exercise success plus safe failure through the public semantic surface and retain secret-free structured logs with scenario/seed, fixture/source root, authority/privacy, transition sequence, injected schedule/fault, budgets/observed work, outcome/error identity, decision/output digests, proof handles, cleanup/obligation state, and an exact reproduction command. No log may contain raw private media, credentials, or unbounded payloads.
acceptance_criteria:
- The exact named tree and multiplicities are encoded in typed construction/ownership APIs and a machine-checkable topology fixture.
- Illegal parentage, double ownership, detached work, authority broadening, and parent-finalize-before-child-drain are rejected with stable errors.
- Cancellation/panic/crash schedules at every node leave all descendants terminal or explicitly indeterminate and satisfy FORMAL-001/INV-006.
- Unit tests cover every parent-child edge and authority field; model/property tests prove one owner and monotone narrowing.
- An e2e property shutdown starts sensor/event/model/alert work, cancels at controlled cut points, and logs the complete drain/obligation/quiescence proof.

title: Validate BudgetVector finite nonnegative quantities at every construction and decode boundary
description:
## Finding and impact

The present Rust skeleton exposes budget quantities as public f64 fields. That permits negative values, NaN, positive or negative infinity, and arithmetic results that are unordered or non-finite. These are not harmless representation quirks: budget comparison is an authority decision. A NaN can make every ordinary comparison false; a negative amount can turn consumption into replenishment; infinity can erase a bound. Such values can therefore corrupt admission, degradation, accounting, receipt generation, serialization, replay, and cross-platform determinism.

This bug owns the representation and validation contract. It must not be papered over by checking one CLI caller or clamping bad values, because values can enter through construction, schema decode, migrations, persisted records, network envelopes, tests, and future APIs.

## Required implementation contract

- Replace or encapsulate freely constructible floating quantities with a validated representation, or make all fields private and force a single checked constructor/decoder.
- Define the valid domain for every budget dimension: finite and greater than or equal to zero, plus any explicit upper bound established by the normative registry. Do not invent sentinel infinities.
- Reject negative zero only if the canonical numeric/schema contract requires it; otherwise normalize it deterministically and test the chosen representation.
- Give negative, NaN, infinity, overflow, underflow, and incompatible-unit failures stable typed identities with dimension/path context.
- Make addition, subtraction, reservation, release, comparison, consumption, remaining-budget calculation, and projection checked. Consumption may not increase remaining authority.
- Specify canonical serialization and digest behavior so semantically equal valid budgets have identical bytes and hashes across platforms.
- Validate on every untrusted or persisted decode path, including migrations and universal request/response envelopes. Invalid historical data must produce an explicit repair/quarantine result, never silent normalization.
- Preserve authority-plane separation: a model or cognition result cannot mint or enlarge a budget.
- Ensure redacted logs identify the field/dimension, stable error, request/session correlation, and validation stage without recording secrets, prompts, evidence payloads, or raw untrusted documents.

## Failure and compatibility considerations

Existing fixtures may have relied on unconstrained struct literals. Migrate them through checked constructors. If a wire or storage schema currently admits arbitrary IEEE-754 values, version the validation semantics and provide a deterministic compatibility/migration decision. Do not silently reinterpret already signed or hashed invalid bytes.

The implementation must remain unsafe-free, cancellation-aware at any I/O boundary, and compatible with the repository's explicit ContractBasis and AgentResponseEnvelope rules.

## Required proof

Unit tests cover every dimension and boundary value, including zero, ordinary valid values, negative values, both infinities, NaN payload variants, arithmetic overflow, over-consumption, and deterministic normalization. Property tests assert construction closure, monotone consumption, no authority creation, stable ordering, and encode/decode round trips for all accepted values. Schema and migration tests inject invalid persisted and wire forms. Differential/reference tests compare the optimized representation with a simple exact checked model.

An end-to-end script must exercise a real agent-facing request through decode, budget admission, consumption, response receipt, and replay. It must also inject each invalid class and prove a stable nonzero exit/error envelope, unchanged authority, no partial effect, and a retained redacted proof bundle. Logs must contain stable event/error IDs, budget dimension, before/after digests for valid transitions, consumed/remaining quantities, degradation choice, correlation IDs, and proof handles.
acceptance_criteria: All public and deserialization construction paths reject negative, NaN, and infinite budget quantities with stable typed errors; arithmetic is checked and deterministic; unit, property, decode, envelope, CLI/e2e, and structured-log tests retain proof without leaking sensitive inputs.

title: FSS-022 — Implement typed budgets and pressure propagation
description:
## Outcome

Implement typed budgets and pressure propagation. Deliver this as a complete vertical contract in the owned runtime and authority work package, not as a placeholder, mock-only path, or source-presence claim.

## Background and system role

This task contributes Asupersync Cx/regions, budgets, obligations, capabilities, leases, cancellation drain, effect phases, and laboratory schedule control. It must compose with one EvidenceAnchor/EvidenceDeltaBatch universe and preserve authority, cognition, and effect-plane ownership. Relevant non-negotiable invariants include INV-006, INV-007, INV-040, INV-058, INV-061.

## Required technical contract

Start with a deterministic reference implementation and typed state machine; expose explicit success, expected failure, cancellation, panic/quarantine, stale-generation, budget, and indeterminate outcomes before adding optimization or concurrency.

Every public or durable object needs stable identity, explicit owner, bounded inputs/outputs, compatibility generation, validity/invalidators, cost row, privacy/capability projection, and structured errors with safe retry/rebase/reconcile/repair guidance. Optimization is admitted only after a simple oracle and same-semantic proof exist.

## Failure and recovery semantics

Cover malformed or missing input, duplicate/reordered work, stale anchors/generations, cancellation at each publication/effect boundary, crash/restart, partial I/O, resource pressure, unavailable dependencies, privacy/capability revocation, and incompatible versions. Preserve valid partial evidence but never upgrade an uncertain, stale, uncovered, redacted, or indeterminate state to success.

## Verification and diagnostic logging

Add focused unit and property tests plus deterministic reference, differential/metamorphic, fault/cancellation/crash, integration, and end-to-end scenarios appropriate to the task. Every scenario emits bounded structured logs containing scenario and seed, source/fixture root, ContractBasis and generations, authority/capability/privacy scope, injected schedule/fault, transition sequence, budgets and observed work, outcome/error identity, semantic/decision digest, proof handles, and minimal reproduction command. Logs must be secret-free and avoid raw private media.

## Completion boundary

Qualification is INT-AS-001, TEST-SCHEDULE-001, and GATE-020. Completion requires implementation, success/failure semantics, migrations/compatibility, operation-cost evidence, tests, retained proof bundle, registry/schema/status updates, and user/agent-facing documentation to agree.

- Required schemas, registries, migrations, status, documentation, and proof roots agree; no claim exceeds retained evidence.
